Npcgen.postsTheListToTheGms: Posts the list to the GMs.

Effects.diceAgainstAttacksUntilThe: +{attribute} dice against attacks until the next action
Effects.burnsEveryCombatTurnUntil: burns every Combat Turn until put out
Effects.lostOnAnyActionButAiming: lost on any action but aiming or attacking
Effects.tnToEveryTestUntil: +{withdrawalTn} TN to every test until the next dose

Interface.sheetLayoutYourChoiceFor: Sheet layout (your choice, for every sheet)
Interface.needsAActionNotEnough: needs a {cost} action: not enough left this phase

Demo.thisDemoShowsTheSr2e: This demo shows the SR2e system at work. It made four runners ({sam}, {mage}, {decker}, {rigger}), a gang ({gang}), a corporate host ({host}), a secured building ({site}), a safehouse ({safehouse}), a car and a drone, and the scene {scene}. Everything is in the folders named "Demo (SR2e)".
Demo.openTheSceneFromThe: Open the scene from the Scenes sidebar (right-click, {view}), or {activate} it to bring your players along.
Demo.toLetPlayersTryIt: To let players try it, give each one a runner: GM panel ({keys}), {setup} tab, {players}. The runners are full characters, made with the NPC generator at Threat Level 3.
Demo.thePagesOfThisJournal: The pages of this journal each try one part of the system. The in-game guide ({keys}, or the book button on any sheet) explains every screen.
Demo.whenYouAreDoneGm: When you are done: GM panel, {setup}, {remove}. It deletes only what the demo made.
Demo.theGangWaitsInThe: The gang waits in the lot. Select {sam}'s token, then target a ganger (hover over its token and press {key}).
Demo.startACombatSelectThe: Start a combat: select the tokens, right-click one to open its HUD and press the combat button (crossed swords), then {begin} in the combat tracker. Roll initiative with {keys} (or the GM panel's Combat tab for the NPCs). SR2 initiative passes are handled by the tracker.
Demo.onSSheetPress: On {sam}'s sheet, press {attack} (or a weapon's attack button). The dialog shows the target number with every modifier the system found (range, light, wounds, cover...), each one switchable. The chat card then offers the target {defend} and {resist}: damage staging and the condition monitor follow by themselves.
Demo.tryTheCombatPoolA: Try the Combat Pool, a Karma re-roll on a card, and full defense. A wounded character gets the wound modifier on every test.
Demo.knowsAFewSpells: {mage} knows a few spells. On the sheet's Magic tab, cast one at a ganger: choose the Force and the Spell Pool dice. The card shows the hits, the target's resistance, and then the {drain} test, Stun or Physical by the Force.
Demo.sustainASpellToSee: Sustain a spell to see it in the sustained list and its penalty, or conjure a spirit with the Summon quick action.
Demo.hasACyberdeck: {decker} has a cyberdeck. On the sheet's Matrix tab, press {jackIn} and pick the host {host}.
Demo.eachSystemOperationIsA: Each system operation is a test against the host's subsystem: failures raise the security tally, and at the sheaf's steps IC comes out and alerts go up. Watch the host's sheet (the GM sees its tally and sheaf). Jack out before the IC gets nasty.
Demo.hasAControlRig: {rigger} has a control rig, the vehicle {car} and the drone {drone} (the drone already subscribed). A player who plays the rigger also needs to own them: right-click each in the Actors sidebar, {configure}.
Demo.onTheSheetSRigging: On the sheet's Rigging tab, {takeControls} of the vehicle (drive it or jump in); {subscribe} adds more drones.
Demo.jumpedInTheRiggerUses: Jumped in, the rigger uses the Control Pool and the vehicle's sensors; a Driving test comes from the Drive quick action. To try a chase, open the vehicle's sheet and press {giveChase} with another vehicle as the quarry (make one with the NPC generator: a rigger comes with vehicles).
Demo.theBuildingOnTheRight: The building on the right is the site {site}. Its west door is locked by a keypad maglock, and there is a camera and a door alarm. Open the site's sheet to see the devices, the security tally and its steps, the alert and the response.
Demo.toGetInUseThe: To get in, use the {bypass} quick action on {decker}'s or {rigger}'s sheet (they know Electronics) and pick the door's maglock: success unlocks the door on the map. A failure raises the site's tally; at 3 a guard looks, at 6 the alarm calls the response, at 9 the building locks down.
Demo.theRunnersSafehouseIs: The runners' safehouse is {safehouse}: its sheet shows the upkeep, the options and who lives there.
Demo.everyCharacterSheetHasA: Every character sheet has a {print} button (a printer) in its title bar: a light-on-ink printout, or a PDF.
Demo.foundABugTheGuide: Found a bug? The guide has a {report} button: copy the text into a GitHub issue. Nothing is sent by itself.
Demo.theAlarmGoesOffSecurity: The alarm goes off; security is called
Demo.twoCorporateSecurityGuardsIn: Two corporate security guards in a patrol car

Guide.gmOnly: This part of the guide is for the GM.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.b1: This guide explains the SR2e system's screens: what to click and what happens. It does not teach the rules. For those, use your SR2 rulebook.
gettingStarted.b2: The system, this guide included, was built with AI (Anthropic's Claude) under human direction; see Credits and licence.
gettingStarted.b3: Open your character from the Actors sidebar. A character sheet has a header (picture, name, metatype), the summary bar, the status strip, a row of tabs, the toolbar and the open tab below them. That is the Tabs layout; you can pick another (see Layouts).

b4.i1: Main: attributes, derived values, the condition monitor and skills.
b4.i2: Current: a read-only page of where the character stands now.
b4.i4: Effects: everything acting on the character right now.
b4.i5: Magic: tradition, spells, foci, spirits. Only for characters with Magic, spells, powers or foci.
b4.i6: Matrix: only when the character owns a cyberdeck or a program.
b4.i7: Rigging: only when the character can rig.
b4.i9: Upkeep: money, lifestyle, Karma, things under way, contacts, the ledger.
b4.i10: Creation: the creation wizard, then the creation record and the advancement log.
b4.i11: Bio: edges and flaws, reputation, biography and notes.

gettingStarted.b5: A new character starts with the creation wizard. A small ? beside a heading on a sheet opens this guide at the topic for that part, and the book icon in a sheet's title bar (Guide) opens the whole guide. The guide window lists every topic on the left, and its search box finds words in all of them.
gettingStarted.b6: For a guided walk through the sheet, open Foundry's Settings tab, then Tours: SR2e: your character sheet and SR2e: adding things.

tools.title: All the tools
tools.b1: Every SR2e tool is in one window, SR2e tools. For everyone: the guide, your sheet, Defend, Resist, rolling initiative, ending your turn, the newest chat card, roll privacy, your look and settings, the tours and Report a bug. For the GM also: the GM panel and its tabs (the calculator, undo and the log, requests, setup), the NPC generator, awards, the house rules, the Skill Web, the macros and the GM panel tour. Each tool has a line on what it does, and its hotkey if it has one.
tools.b2: Open it with Alt+T, the SR2e tools button at the bottom of the Actors sidebar, the SR2e tools button at the top of this guide's topic list, or the toolbox in Foundry's toolbar on the left (shown while a scene is on the canvas). The toolbox group also has the most used tools as buttons of their own; its first tool selects tokens as usual.
tools.b3: The guide itself opens with Alt+H, the book icon in the title bar of every SR2e sheet, or the small ? beside a heading (that part's topic). Shortcuts, hotkeys and token actions lists every hotkey.

rulesV079.title: Rules updated in v0.79.0
rulesV079.b1: v0.79.0 corrected rules to follow the official SR2 rulebooks (the core rules and Rigger 2). The GM can put any of them back under the GM's house rules (search for the subject; the old choice is the second one).

b2.i1: Ranged combat: recoil follows the book's table (a second semi-automatic shot +1, each burst +3, a second burst in the same phase +6, full auto +1 per round fired). You can't add more Combat Pool dice to an attack than your skill rating; resisting damage has no limit. Reloading a clip takes both Simple Actions (remove, then insert; a smartgun ejects for free); belts, revolvers and other feeds take a Complex Action. Smartlink II is −2, like Smartlink I. Flechette adds a damage level only against no armor. Thrown grenades scatter 1D6 m (aerodynamic 2D6), launched ones 3D6. Rifles, the LMG, the taser, the missile launcher, bows, crossbows, shuriken and grenades use the book's range table.
b2.i2: Surprise: the surprise turn goes in order of surprise successes, and you can't attack someone who rolled more successes than you.
b2.i3: Seeing: minimal light is +6 for normal eyes. Natural (metatype) low-light and thermographic vision are better than cybereyes. Glare, mist and heavy smoke are new choices, and rain and fog count as light or heavy smoke.
b2.i4: Melee: the shorter reach takes +1 per point on its own roll; superior position (−1) is on.
b2.i5: Notice: tick every sight row that applies (very small, partly hidden, brightly colored, very obvious, not obvious); the result reads in the book's four steps.
b2.i6: Healing: Physical damage heals in stages, one wound level per Rest test (days, not hours); a failed first self-recovery test means you need a doctor. First aid is TN 4/6/8/10, +4 without a medkit, +2 for a magician patient.
b2.i7: Social: Etiquette, Leadership and Negotiation roll only your side, against the target's attribute; one success gets you what you asked. Pick what you want on the book's scale, from "advantageous to them" (−2) to "disastrous to them" (+6). A suspicious NPC is +2.
b2.i8: Karma: an active skill costs the new rating × 2, a concentration × 1.5 and a specialization × 1, whatever your attribute.
b2.i9: Magic: your Spell Pool is your Sorcery rating (plus an active power focus); at most your Magic rating of it goes on a spell's success test, any amount on drain. Spell defense dice you use are spent until the pools refresh. An ally's spell defense can protect you when you share a player, a fight or a scene (and aren't on opposite sides), or when its mage covers you: target your tokens and press Cover targets next to the spell defense box.
b2.i10: Vehicles: driving over the Speed rating is +1. Crashes and rams hurt by speed (up to 20 m/turn Light, 60 Moderate, 200 Serious, faster Destroyed). Fixed mounts and turrets halve recoil; a pintle compensates 2, the new ring mount 6. The Sensor dialog has the Rigger 2 rows (line of sight, terrain, a concealing spirit), and sensor-enhanced gunnery rolls Gunnery + half the Sensor against the target's Signature. A repair fixes all the damage in 16 hours per box ÷ successes.
b2.i11: Rigging: dumped from a remote control deck (your drone destroyed, or your link jammed), you resist (deck rating + 4)S Stun with Body. Radio ranges follow the Rigger 2 flux table (250 m at 0, up to 25 km at 9); a deck with no signal of its own has flux 2.

rulesUrr.title: The Unified Rules Revamp (alternate rules)
rulesUrr.b1: The GM chooses the world's Rules source (Configure Settings, or the GM panel's Setup tab). SR2E Book Rules is the default and is not changed by any of this. SR2E Unified Rules Revamp is the GM's alternate ruleset: the Unified Rules Revamp follows the community document Shadowrun Classic: Unified Rule Revamp (v1.2), with a few house rules where it is silent. The GM's own house rules still win over it, and the house rules window marks every row it changes (search for "revamp"). A switch reaches every player at once.
rulesUrr.b2: Using the Unified Rules Revamp changes these:

b3.i1: Tests and Karma: skill and attribute cards point out critical successes; the roll dialogs have a Difficulty list (knowledge skills get the knowledge table); ties on opposed perception and social tests go to whoever made the test; you can buy extra dice from your Karma Pool (one point a die). Metahumans start with a Karma Pool of 2, and each award puts its first point into the pool. Attributes cost the new rating × 1.5 (past the racial maximum, with the GM's leave, × 3), languages × 1; your native language is free at Intelligence + 2. Training takes Karma × 8 hours. Magic is capped at Essence rounded down.
b3.i2: Combat: you don't dodge gunfire: Defend puts your Combat Pool dice into the resistance test, and if their successes beat the attacker's it is a clean miss. Damage stages on the resistance test (the attack's successes against yours, 2 either way per level). Full defense in melee adds no dice. A hit that hurts calls for a knockdown test. Initiative ties go to Reaction, then natural Reaction. Shotguns fire slugs unless loaded with shot. Strong shooters take less recoil; tracers only help full auto. Heavy armor costs Combat Pool dice; a second layer adds half. Charging is +1 Power; graded cover, running and sprinting targets and more are in the Attack dialog.
b3.i3: Health: Stun past a full track goes onto Physical box for box. Bleeding is a box every 10 minutes, and death comes one box past Overflow. First aid lowers a wound one level (Deadly: stabilise only) and shows the treatment time; a better healer can try again. A trauma patch needs a Body test. Stun recovery is the better of Body and Willpower vs 2. A Deadly wound heals only in intensive care; a magician treated without the +2 makes a Magic loss test. Climbing, jumping, swimming and falling use Fitness; trolls run at Quickness × 2.
b3.i4: Social and perception: the Perceive and Sneak dialogs list sound, smell, touch and taste rows; Negotiation is against Intelligence; haggling moves the price 10% per net success, and the seller rolls against your Intelligence; visible armor in a luxury setting is +2.
b3.i5: Magic: you roll the spell's Force (plus Spell Pool) to cast; you sustain at most your Sorcery rating in spells; a disaster on casting is +2 drain TN; exclusive spells hit as if 2 Force higher, fetish ones 1. Summoning above your Charisma gives Physical drain; one nature spirit at a time. Astral initiative is 2 × Intelligence + 15 + 1D6. Wards use Sorcery. The Magic loss test also loses a point on a roll equal to your Magic.
b3.i6: Vehicles and rigging: Control Pool dice on a driving test are capped at your skill, and don't go on gunnery or sensor tests (shoot with the Combat Pool), but do help your vehicle resist damage. Rigger feedback comes only from Serious (6M) or Deadly (6S) hits, resisted with Body. Small arms lose Power by Body + Armor. Passengers are hurt only when shot at, or in a crash or ram. A damaged vehicle is slower. A sensor lock is a Complex Action.
b3.i7: Drones and security: intercepting a drone link needs a remote control deck (break the encryption first); card-reader casings are twice as hard; a passkey and a sequencer roll against the lock; a weapon detector finds everything no better than its highest die; dump shock leaves you disoriented (+2 TN) for a few turns.

rulesUrr.b4: Rules the Revamp describes but the system can't run (for example the alert track, an astral combat pool, team tactics) are listed for the GM in docs/VERIFY.md.

sheetTools.title: Edit mode, Play mode and the toolbar
sheetTools.b1: Under the tabs is a toolbar with a Find on this sheet… box, the layout picker (Layouts) and, for the owner, the Edit / Play button.

b2.i1: Edit mode: add, delete and change everything.
b2.i2: Play mode hides the add, delete and duplicate buttons and locks the name, the metatype, base ratings and the number boxes on rows. The attribute Mod column, gear quantities, pools and the condition monitor still work. Click the button to switch.

sheetTools.b3: Edit or Play is remembered for each character on this computer; a new sheet opens in Edit mode.
sheetTools.b4: Type in the find box to hide the rows that don't match. Each tab shows how many rows it found, and folded sections open to show what matches. <kbd>Esc</kbd> clears the box.
sheetTools.b5: Click a heading to fold its section away, and again to open it. The sheet remembers what you folded.
sheetTools.b6: Some rows have a number box: a skill's rating, a spell's Force, a gear quantity. Change it there without opening the item. The small − and + beside a number step it by one, and the scroll wheel changes the number while the box has the cursor (Configure Settings: Sheets: − / + on numbers). Once a character has a creation record (or, with the approval queue on, once they are out of the wizard), a player can't raise a rating this way: use Spend Karma. Lowering still works, and the GM can type anything (see Creation record).
sheetTools.b7: Row icons: the pin puts the row in the pin bar at the top of the sheet (click the row's pin again to take it off); the pencil opens the item (so does the name on most rows, but a skill's name rolls it); the copy icon duplicates it; the trash can deletes it.
sheetTools.b8: You can also drag an item from the Items sidebar or a compendium onto the sheet.
sheetTools.b9: Reference (the open book in the title bar of a character or NPC sheet) opens a pane beside the sheet that searches the Catalogue, the guide and the rules interpretations at once. Click a result to open it. Drag a Catalogue entry onto the sheet to open the shop with it ticked: you still find and buy it as usual (spells and adept powers open Learn).

summaryBar.title: The summary bar
summaryBar.b1: The summary bar sits under the header on character and NPC sheets. The monitor, pools and initiative are in the status strip just below it.

b2.i1: Grey chips list things acting on the character (statuses, sustained spells, encumbrance and so on).
b2.i2: The pin bar: rows you pinned, one click to use.
b2.i3: Setup: when something on the sheet looks wrong (an attribute at 0, ware not installed) this line lists it. Click an entry to go to it.

summaryBar.b3: The quick buttons: Attack, First aid, Rest, Perceive, Notice, Pay (negotiate a job's pay; character sheets only), Sneak, Athletics, Search and Social. Others show only when they fit:

b4.i1: Magic: Cast with spells, Summon with Conjuring, Assense and Astral attack when astral.
b4.i2: Trouble: Reload with a magazine weapon, Clear jam for a jammed weapon, Put out fire while burning, Stand up while prone, Break free while someone holds you.
b4.i3: Combat: Initiative when there is a combat; in a running combat Full defense and Hold (grab and pin the targeted token); in your action phase Delay (then Act now, and Done when the delayed action is over).
b4.i4: Groups: Rally with Leadership (rally a broken group), Morale for a group or an NPC with a Professional Rating.
b4.i5: Matrix and rigging: Jack in / Jack out with a deck, Hitch / Unhitch (ride a decker's hitcher jack), Drive at the controls of a vehicle, Drone link when there are vehicles, Jam with a jammer, Bypass when a site has locks.

summaryBar.b5: Hover a button to see what it does.

layouts.title: Layouts, the status strip and your turn
layouts.b1: Each player picks how character, NPC and spirit sheets look for them: the layout picker in the sheet's toolbar, or Configure Settings: Sheets: layout. It changes every sheet you open, not the other players'.

b2.i1: Tabs (the default): one tab at a time.
b2.i2: Combat column: the tabs plus an always-open column on the right with Defense (Resist, Full defense in a running combat, First aid), Weapons (Attack, or a button per firing mode for a firearm; reload; rounds left; the hand icon draws a holstered weapon; an Unarmed row), Spells (Cast) and Actions (the quick buttons). In a narrow window the column moves under the strip.
b2.i3: Compact: no tab bar; every tab is a folding section in one column, for narrow windows. Main and Combat start open. Click a section's header (or press Enter on it) to fold or open it; the sheet remembers. The find box still finds rows in folded sections.

layouts.b3: The status strip stays at the top of the sheet with the tabs while you scroll:

b4.i1: A small condition monitor (P Physical, S Stun, OF Overflow, in the same wound groups as the monitor), the wound TN modifier and the character's state.
b4.i2: Init: Reaction + dice before the roll, the initiative this pass in a running combat.
b4.i3: The pools as pips: C Combat, Sp Spell, H Hacking, Ct Control (only while jumped in), KP Karma; a pool shows only when the character has it. Filled pips are dice left (the number beside them is exact); click a pip to set the number (see Dice pools).
b4.i4: The readied weapon (the one you last attacked with, else a pinned one, else the first ready gun) with its mode and rounds left. Click it to attack; Shift-click to attack at once with its remembered choices.

layouts.b5: Your turn: in a running combat, when it is your character's action phase, the strip says so. Unless the GM's house rule Actions per phase is off, it shows a pip for each action left, and buttons that need more than you have left are greyed out (hover one for why). Warn (the default) lets you click and warns you; block stops the click (the GM can always click). A projecting magician's or an unmaterialized spirit's physical actions are greyed the same way.
layouts.b6: In Foundry's combat tracker, your own combatants show their pools, and get a shield button for full defense (out of turn it costs initiative) and Delay in your action phase (then Act now and Done), like the sheet's quick buttons.
layouts.b7: Other choices for yourself in Configure Settings, section Look and layout: Windows: remember size and place (SR2e's sheets and windows open where you left them; dialogs don't) and Notifications: group bursts (several notices at once become one, and a repeat shows ×2, ×3).

rolling.title: Rolling a test
rolling.b1: Click a name to roll it: an attribute's name in the Attributes table, a skill's name, a weapon's Attack, a spell's Cast, a power's Use. A dialog opens.
rolling.b2: The dialog has your choices on the left and, on the right, the target number (TN) with a preview of every modifier that goes into it (in a narrow window the preview goes underneath). Modifiers the system found by itself (wounds, range, light, smoke and so on) each have a tick box: untick one to switch it off for this roll only. Type any other modifier in the modifier box. Where a pool can help, there is a box for pool dice. The preview follows what you change. Number boxes have − / + and take the scroll wheel.
rolling.b3: Click the big button with the dice icon at the bottom (its label says what it does, for example Cast). The result goes to the chat as a card with the dice, the successes and buttons for the next step (see Chat cards).
rolling.b4: The dialog remembers what you chose last time for the same spell, skill or summoning (Force, pool dice, the specialization box), on this computer: Configure Settings, Roll dialogs: remember my last choices. Weapons always remember their firing mode and options. Cancelling doesn't store anything.
rolling.b5: Skill dialogs have a Use specialization box; the Sneak dialog has Use the specialization too, and the people watching count their own Perception specialization and gear by themselves.
rolling.b6: Shift-click a roll button to skip the dialog and roll at once with its defaults. A spell or skill rolls without your remembered choices; a weapon uses its remembered firing mode and pool dice, but never fires twice.
rolling.b7: How many dice you roll and what the TN should be come from the rules: see your SR2 rulebook. You choose who sees each kind of test you roll (Configure Settings: Set roll privacy, under Roll privacy by kind of test). Foundry's chat mode follows the mode picked under the chat box. Cards someone else must answer (Defend, Resist, a blast) are always public.

targeting.title: Targets and automatic modifiers
targeting.b1: Before you attack, cast or use a power on someone, target their token: hover over it and press <kbd>T</kbd> (Foundry's usual way). You can target more than one.
targeting.b2: With a target picked, the dialog measures the range from your token, checks the line of sight, the light at the target, smoke between you and similar things, and puts them in the preview as modifiers. Untick any that don't fit what is really happening.
targeting.b3: Weapons with a blast and area spells have a circle icon on their row: click it and place the area on the map. Everyone inside becomes your target.
targeting.b4: Take Aim (the bullseye on a weapon row) aims at the targeted token. Each aim posts a card with the TN it gives; the next attack at that target shows it as Aimed in the preview.
targeting.b5: Against a target that is invisible to you, the system rolls your test to see through it first and posts that card before the attack or spell: a Perception test against twice the caster's successes. Thermographic eyes see through plain (mana) Invisibility.

chatCards.title: Chat cards: Defend, Resist and Apply
chatCards.b1: Most tests post a card with buttons for what comes next. Only the owner of the character named on the button, or the GM, can use it.

b2.i1: Defend: on an attack card, for the target. It opens the defense dialog with pool dice. Against a melee attack you pick the weapon you fight back with (with a Counterattack to subdue box where it applies). Once you have defended, the button is greyed for you, even after a reload; the GM gets an Already defended question before a second defense. A vehicle defends with its driver's Combat Pool dice, or the Control Pool of a rigger jumped into it.
b2.i2: Resist (or Resist damage): after a hit, the damage resistance test. The condition monitor changes by itself.
b2.i3: Resist on a spell or power card: the target's resistance test.
b2.i4: Apply (GM): your test changed something only the GM may change (a host, a site, a patient you don't own). The GM clicks it to make the change.
b2.i5: Other buttons follow from the test, for example Detonate for a blast, a Knockdown test, Buy after a find test, Use again for a repeating power, Rammer's damage on the defense card after a ram. Hover a button for details.

chatCards.b3: A card that a Karma re-roll, a bought success or the GM's new TN has replaced says Replaced and its buttons stop working: use the newer card. A card the GM re-scored says so; the cards that already followed from the old one aren't changed.
chatCards.b4: Attack, damage and spell cards list their targets: click a name to show its token on the map. On a purchase card, the buyer can drag the item onto a sheet.
chatCards.b5: Cards from other players. Anyone can post a chat card with any data, so the system checks who posted it:

b6.i1: Routine tests that another player's attack forces on your character (Defend, Resist, a knockdown, a toxin, catching fire, taking cover) go ahead at once when the card comes from that player's own character.
b6.i2: Anything else, such as something costly or lasting (Magic loss, cyberware or deck damage, a disease, a crash), first asks you in an A card from another player window. It lists what will happen, read from the card's data: go ahead only if it matches what really happened.
b6.i3: A card that doesn't say which character it comes from does nothing (nothing done).

chatCards.b7: Reading a card at a glance (colours as seen by whoever rolled):

b8.i1: Solid green with ✔: it worked (a success, a dodge, damage resisted).
b8.i2: Solid red with ✖: it didn't (a failure, a miss, a hit taken, damage taken).
b8.i3: Black with ⚠: a disaster. Purple with ⇄: a counterattack.
b8.i4: An amber outline: nothing settled yet, for example an attack waiting for the defense.
b8.i5: The success count is green with successes and red at none. On a contest (haggling, sneaking, perceiving and so on) the winner's count is green, the loser's red, a tie amber, and the result line is boxed.
b8.i6: The card's right edge repeats the outcome; its left edge and the strip at the top show the kind of test.

chatCards.b9: Karma buttons are explained in Karma Pool on chat cards.
chatCards.b10: When an attack or damage comes at a character you own, the system can ask you at once (Configure Settings: When you are attacked or hit: Open the dialog, Notify me, Do nothing). Later (use the card) leaves it on the card. One card asks about at most 12 targets; beyond that you get one notice to use the card's buttons. Fold dice on chat cards folds the dice under the summary line: click to open them.
chatCards.b11: The strip at the top of a card is coloured by the kind of test: red for combat, violet for magic, green for the Matrix, orange for rigging, gold (a sandy brown in the Corp theme) for the street, teal for health and healing. The big number is the successes; dice that hit are lit, 1s are marked. With Dice colours on chat cards set to colourblind-safe, blue and orange (with the symbols) take the place of green and red everywhere on the card.

look.title: Your look: theme, colours and text size
look.b1: Each player picks the look of SR2e's own windows and chat cards for themselves (Foundry's sidebar keeps its own look). In Configure Settings, SR2e:

b2.i1: Look: theme: Street (dark gunmetal, the default), Corp (a shaded light theme) or High contrast.
b2.i2: Look: colour preset: the accent colour (Gunmetal cyan, Phosphor green, Magenta or Amber).
b2.i3: Look: window opacity (%): 50 to 100. 100 is solid and easiest to read; lower lets the map show through.
b2.i4: Look: text size (%): 90 to 130 inside SR2e's windows and cards.
b2.i5: Look: reduced motion: no glows or flashes. Your computer's reduced-motion setting is always honoured too.
b2.i6: Dice colours on chat cards: default (green and grey), colourblind-safe (blue and orange, with shapes as well as colour) or high contrast (black and white). They work with every theme and also colour the outcomes.

look.b3: These sit in the section Look and layout, with the layout settings, except Dice colours on chat cards, which is under Rolls, dice and chat. The other sections are Rolls, dice and chat, Tokens and the map, GM and world and Other.
look.b4: More choices for yourself in Configure Settings: Floating damage numbers (boxes of damage and healing float over tokens), Turn pings (a ping on the token whose turn it is), Sound cues (off by default: a sound on your turn, when one of your characters is attacked or hit, and on a disaster; set the volume and the sound files below it) and, with the Dice So Nice module, Dice So Nice: SR2e colours.
look.b5: The GM can name a Portrait folder (for example avatars): a character named Rook then takes avatars/Rook.webp (or .png, .jpg) as its picture, as long as it still has the default picture. With Portraits for tokens too (on by default) it becomes the token picture as well. A picture you set by hand is kept. A portrait found by name replaces the system's default art.

karmaPool.title: Karma Pool on chat cards
karmaPool.b1: If the character has a Karma Pool, their test cards get Karma buttons:

b2.i1: Re-roll N failures (Karma X): rolls the failed dice again. Each re-roll of the same test costs more.
b2.i2: Avoid disaster: on a roll where every die shows 1.
b2.i3: Buy a success: when the test has at least one success. The label says permanent when the point is gone for good rather than back at the next refresh.

karmaPool.b3: On an attack, use Karma before the target defends: once they have, the attack card's Karma buttons refuse.
karmaPool.b4: Each re-roll or bought success makes a new card and the old one is marked Replaced. A re-roll carries through: a re-rolled attack gives a fresh Defend button, a re-rolled resistance test corrects the condition monitor. If the thing changed in between, it is left alone.
karmaPool.b5: Contest and street cards (haggle, fence, legwork, find, sneak, perceive, social tests, negotiating pay) get these buttons for each side that has a Karma Pool, with the side's name on the button. You can use your character's side even on a card the GM rolled.
karmaPool.b6: Karma Pool left shows under Derived on the Main tab. The circular arrow beside it refreshes the pool.

pools.title: Dice pools
pools.b1: The pools are the Combat Pool, Spell Pool, Hacking Pool (Matrix), Control Pool (rigging) and Karma Pool. The status strip shows each as pips; click a pip to set how many are left (clicking the last filled pip takes one die off).
pools.b2: A test dialog that can take pool dice has a box for them. What you use comes off what is left. The Main tab shows the Combat Pool spent; the Matrix and Rigging tabs show theirs, with a box to correct the spent number.
pools.b3: An encephalon gives a small Task Pool for Intelligence, knowledge and Build/Repair skills: the skill dialog has a box for it (used up only in combat). An adept's Combat Sense adds to the Combat Pool, and a power focus adds its rating to the Spell Pool.
pools.b4: The Combat, Spell, Hacking, Control and Task Pools refill when a combat starts and at each new Combat Turn. The GM can also refill them from the GM panel (Party tab: Refresh pools). The Karma Pool doesn't refill with them: use the circular arrow beside Karma Pool left on the Main tab, or the GM's Refresh Karma Pools. A house rule can refill Karma Pools by themselves at the start of each session or when a combat ends.
pools.b5: On the Current tab, Initiative and pools lists the initiative (and Matrix or rigged initiative) and each pool, read only. Your combatants in the combat tracker show their pools too.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts, hotkeys and token actions

b1.i1: Shift-click a roll button (on a sheet, a chat card, the token HUD or the GM panel) to skip the dialog.
b1.i2: <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>D</kbd>: Defend against the newest attack on a character you own that you haven't defended yet.
b1.i3: <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd>: Resist the newest damage to a character you own.
b1.i5: <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd>: roll initiative for your tokens that have none yet.
b1.i6: <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>: open the sheet of your selected token (or of your character).
b1.i7: <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>: go to the newest chat card that has a button (the keyboard focus moves to its first button).
b1.i10: Alt+T: open the SR2e tools window, with every tool in one place.
b1.i11: Drag a row (a weapon, a spell, a skill, a critter power) onto Foundry's hotbar to make a macro that uses it.

shortcuts.b2: The SR2e Macros compendium (Compendium Packs sidebar) has ready macros: SR2 test… (type a test such as Firearms tn 5), Attack, Cast a spell, Perception, Full defense and Roll initiative for your selected token, and Defend against the newest attack. Drag one to your hotbar. The others (the GM panel, the NPC generator, undo, a smoke cloud, exporting item templates) are for the GM.
shortcuts.b3: Change the keys in Foundry's Configure Controls (they are listed under the system's name there).
shortcuts.b4: Using the keyboard. Every button, link and box on the sheets, in the dialogs, on chat cards and in the GM panel can be reached with Tab (Shift+Tab goes back) and pressed with Enter or Space; Shift+Enter (or Shift+Space) is a Shift-click (a roll without the dialog). The control that has the focus shows a ring around it.

b5.i1: A row of tabs is one stop: the arrow keys move along it and <kbd>Enter</kbd> opens a tab.
b5.i2: Each condition monitor track (Physical, Stun, Overflow) and each pool in the status strip is one stop too: the arrow keys move along its boxes or pips (<kbd>Home</kbd> and <kbd>End</kbd> jump to the ends), and <kbd>Enter</kbd> fills up to that box or sets the pool there.
b5.i3: A heading that folds its section: its small arrow is the fold button (<kbd>Enter</kbd> folds or unfolds it).
b5.i4: A dialog puts the focus in its first field, <kbd>Enter</kbd> rolls and <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes it; the focus then goes back to the button that opened it. After a click changes the sheet, the focus stays on the same control.

shortcuts.b6: Screen readers get a name for every icon button (the same text as its tooltip), the condition monitors and pools read out as, for example, Physical: 3 of 10 boxes, and each box says whether it is filled. With Windows' high-contrast mode on, the focus ring and filled boxes use the system's colours.
shortcuts.b7: Right-click a token to open its HUD. The SR2e buttons are in the left column. On your own token: Attack (pick a weapon), Cast a spell if you know one, and Defend when an attack on you is waiting. On someone else's token: you attacks them, which targets that token and opens your attack (for your selected token, or your assigned character).
shortcuts.b8: Hovering over a token you own shows its pools, monitors, initiative and state (Configure Settings: Pools on token hover).
shortcuts.b9: With the Token Action HUD Core module (it needs socketlib), the HUD lists your SR2e actions: no extra system module is needed.

inlineTests.title: Inline tests and /sr2
inlineTests.b1: A journal page, an item description or a chat message can hold a roll link, for example @SR2Test[Firearms tn 5 mod -1]{Shoot the lock}. It shows as a link with a die. Click it to roll for your selected token (or your character): a small dialog shows the TN, the modifier and pool dice. Shift-click skips the dialog.
inlineTests.b2: In the chat, type /sr2 (or /sr2e) and the same words, for example /sr2 Firearms tn 5 mod -1. It rolls at once (no dialog) for the speaker. A skill the character doesn't have offers to default to its attribute (+4 TN).

b3.i1: What to roll: an attribute (body, qui, wil and so on), perception, a skill's name (in quotes if it could be misread, with a specialization in round brackets), or a number of dice (6).
b3.i2: tn 5: the target number (4 when left out).
b3.i3: mod -1: a TN modifier. Several add up.
b3.i4: pool 2: pool dice (Combat Pool for attributes and skills, extra dice for a bare number of dice).
b3.i5: label Climb the fence: the card's title. Everything after label is the title.

attributes.title: Attributes
attributes.b1: The Attributes table has Base, Racial, Mod, Gear and Total. Type the base ratings in Base (Edit mode). Mod is a temporary modifier and stays editable in Play mode. Racial and Gear fill in by themselves. Untick Add racial modifiers in the header if your base ratings already include them.
attributes.b2: Click an attribute's name to roll it. The plus-in-a-circle icon beside it raises it with Good Karma: hover it for the cost. See Spend Karma.
attributes.b3: Below the table: base Essence, natural Magic, low-light and thermographic vision, Reaction bonus and extra initiative dice, for anything the sheet can't work out from your gear, and Drained/gained and Essence hole when they apply (an Essence hole is filled first by new cyberware).
attributes.b4: Derived shows Essence, Body Index, Magic, Reaction, Initiative, Combat Pool and Spell Pool (left / total) and movement. Below: Combat Pool spent, Karma Pool with its refresh icon, and Good Karma.
attributes.b5: Anyone with Magic (adepts too) also gets the Astral choice (physical, perceiving, projecting). On the astral plane the row shows Astral attack; while projecting, Manifest lets you be seen and heard in the physical world (you can't act there). A projecting magician can't cross the edge of a ward region (the GM's setting). A character who can't go astral is put back to physical.
attributes.b6: A character possessed by a spirit shows it under Derived, with Free to end it. A character who must feed (some infected metahumans) shows the days since their last meal; Feed records a meal.
attributes.b7: The Current tab's Attributes table shows the same values read only: hover a total to see where it comes from. In the Spend Karma window, Attributes lists each raise and its cost.

conditionMonitor.title: Condition monitor
conditionMonitor.b1: Two tracks, Physical and Stun. Click a box to set the damage to that box; click the last filled box again to clear it. Each track is split into its wound groups with a divider and a label: boxes 1–2 +1, 3–5 +2, 6–9 +3 to every target number, then box 10 (D on Physical: dying; KO on Stun: unconscious). The group the damage has reached is underlined.
conditionMonitor.b2: Overflow sits beside Physical: one box per point of the character's Body (one more under the Unified Rules Revamp). It stays grey until the Physical track is full, then turns red and fills with damage past box 10. Filling its last box (marked ✕) means death. Spirits have no overflow. The Matrix tracks (a persona, IC) are grouped the same way, with Crash at the end.
conditionMonitor.b3: The − and + beside each track take off or add one box (past box 10 on Physical, into Overflow). Hovering a box shows which boxes a click would fill or clear. With the keyboard, Tab to a box and press Enter or Space.
conditionMonitor.b4: The state (ok, unconscious, dying, dead) shows beside the heading. A +N beside Stun counts boxes past the track. You can also type the boxes in Physical damage and Stun damage.

b5.i1: Resist Damage: for damage that came without a card. Type the damage code (for example 6M), the armor, and tick Stun if it is Stun.
b5.i2: Hazard: falling, fire, drowning, cold, fatigue, radiation and suffocation (heat and electric shock when the house rules use them).
b5.i3: First aid: on this character, or on the token you target.
b5.i4: Rest and heal: natural healing after rest.

conditionMonitor.b6: Usually you don't touch the boxes: the Resist button on a damage card fills them in. A dying character shows a warning until stabilised with first aid; the system keeps track as game time passes, in or out of combat, and by default won't let them rest and heal until stabilised.

skills.title: Skills
skills.b1: Skills are listed by kind: active, knowledge, language and Build/Repair. A row shows the rating, any concentration and specialization, the linked attribute and the dice you'll roll. Click the name to roll it. Slotted skillsofts show under the active skills. A skill marked martial art (set on its sheet) is used for unarmed attacks in place of Unarmed Combat when rated at least as high.
skills.b2: The + on a heading opens the skill picker for that kind. A kind with no skills has no heading yet: use the + on Active skills and change Kind in the picker. Row icons: raise the skill with Karma (plus-in-a-circle), raise its concentration or specialization (the square icons), pin, edit, delete.
skills.b3: The rating box on a row changes the rating straight away during creation. Afterwards a player raises it with Spend Karma. The Spend Karma window's Skills list shows each skill's next step and cost.

skillPicker.title: The skill picker
skillPicker.b1: The skill picker opens from the + on a skills heading, from the Skills tab of the Add window, and from the + in Spend Karma.

b2.i1: Kind: active, knowledge, language or Build/Repair.
b2.i2: Name: type it, or pick from the list of common skills.
b2.i3: Linked attribute: guessed from the name; change it if the guess is wrong. Knowledge and language skills always use Intelligence.
b2.i4: Rating, Specialization and the specialization's rating (0 means the rating + 1).
b2.i5: Pay: Free (creation, GM gift) or Learn with Good Karma. The cost shows under the form. In creation only Free is offered.

skillPicker.b3: Click Add skill. A skill the character already has is refused: raise it instead. With training time on (the default), a skill learned with Karma starts at 0 and trains to 1. You pay for rating 1 only, whatever Rating you typed. The specialization you gave it is kept. Raise it further with Spend Karma; see Under way.

currentTab.title: The Current tab
currentTab.b1: The Current tab is a read-only page of where the character stands now. The roll buttons are on Main.

b2.i1: Attributes: base, natural and now. Hover a total to see its sources. With a creation record, Since shows the change since creation.
b2.i2: Initiative and pools.
b2.i3: Body: armor, Physical and Stun boxes, wounds, state and metatype.
b2.i4: Karma and money: Good Karma, Karma earned in all, Karma Pool, nuyen and lifestyle. The star opens Spend Karma.

weapons.title: Weapons and armor
weapons.b1: The Armory tab lists your weapons, any cyberweapons, and Unarmed. Each has an Attack button. Firearms also have one button per firing mode they allow.
weapons.b2: Target first (see Targets), then click Attack. The dialog shows the TN preview and boxes for Combat Pool dice and other modifiers. The attack card gives the target a Defend button, and a hit gives a Resist button. Shift-click Attack to skip the dialog. A weapon that may fire twice in a phase has a Fire twice box in the dialog (it spends two simple actions).
weapons.b3: Row icons and buttons, where they fit: ammunition pips and reload (circular arrow), Take Aim (bullseye), place a blast area (circle), suppressive fire, holstered (click to draw), set up a bipod or tripod, Repair… for a broken weapon. A jammed weapon gets a Clear jam quick button in the summary bar.
weapons.b4: Cyberweapons and Unarmed have no edit or delete icons: a cyberweapon is changed on its cyberware's sheet.
weapons.b5: A flash grenade doesn't blind outright: everyone with a clear line to it gets a TN penalty (+6 close up, less with distance, halved by flare compensation) for a few Combat Turns; the card rolls each one's Body to shorten it.
weapons.b6: Armor lists Ballistic / Impact. A piece you aren't wearing says not worn; open it to change that. adds marks a helmet or shield that adds to other armor; parry and conceal show where they apply. Damaged armor shows a minus and a repair icon. The line under the list says what counts against attacks.
weapons.b7: The + on either heading opens the Add window. Vehicle weapons: see Vehicle sheets.
weapons.b8: Each weapon, armor and gear row has a suitcase: click it to leave the thing behind (at the safehouse, in the car). Left behind, it weighs nothing, a search or frisk doesn't find it, and it can't be used, drawn or worn until you carry it again (armor comes off and a weapon is holstered as you leave it). The combat column lists only the weapons you carry.

effects.title: Effects and what is in effect
effects.b1: The Effects tab lists everything acting on the character now, in groups: Condition, Statuses, Combat, Magic, Health, and Matrix and rigging. Rows with a time limit show the time left. The × on a status takes it off.
effects.b2: The Current tab's In effect list shows the same things. On the Gear tab, In effect lists drugs working now, each with a Wear off button. NPC and spirit sheets have the same list in a folded Effects section at the bottom.
effects.b3: Custom tweaks lists every tweak on your items that counts right now, with the item it comes from (see Item sheets).

magic.title: Magic
magic.b1: The Magic tab's Magic section is for magically active characters.

b2.i1: Top row: Tradition; spell defense dice (held back from the Spell Pool) with Cover targets (target your allies' tokens first; with no targets it covers only you), or, for adepts, power points; and buttons for what the character can do: Assense, Force barrier, Dispel, Signatures, Track, Enchant, Quest, Initiate, Ward… (raise a ward by ritual). Only those that apply show. An ally's spell defense protects you only if they cover you, share an owner or a combat with you, or are on your side on the same scene.
b2.i2: The scene environment and background count here (the GM sets them with the pencils), and a running quest with Next stage and × to end it. While projecting, the hours out of the body show against the limit.
b2.i3: Initiate grade and metamagic tick boxes. Adepts initiate too: they see Initiate, their grade and only the techniques an adept can learn (centering and the others the house rules allow), but not Quest, Ward… or Geasa. A centering initiate fills in Centering skill (for example Singing); Center then rolls it before a magical test.
b2.i4: Shamans fill in the totem: its bonuses, its environment and the dice in and away from it, Berserk, Daylight TN and which spirits its conjuring dice help. An elementalist picks an Element.
b2.i5: Geasa: the + adds one; click one to change its words. Untick Met when a geas is broken; the heading shows the Magic lost.
b2.i6: Sustaining: spells you hold and the TN they add. The × drops one. Quicken or Elemental where allowed.
b2.i8: Foci: tick Active; the rating is a box. Bond an unbonded focus for Good Karma. An addiction risk shows with an Addiction test button (the GM's × clears an addiction).
b2.i9: Adept powers: tick Active and set the level. Powers over budget are marked.
b2.i10: Group: your magical group, its strictures, and its grimoire (Learn a spell from it).
b2.i11: Sustaining powers and Under spells and powers (on the Main tab): effects you hold on others and effects on you. The × ends one where you may.

magic.b3: Initiates and other magicians also get, where they apply:

b4.i1: Initiate shows the Good Karma cost and lets you learn a metamagic technique, pick an ordeal (it lowers the cost) and initiate with your group. A deed waits for the GM: the section shows deed pending (the × gives it up, no Karma spent) until the GM confirms it on the card.
b4.i2: Cleanse (lower the background count here, while perceiving or projecting), Divine (a question whispered to the GM) and Invoke (make one of your spirits a great form spirit), for initiates who know the technique. Possess shows while projecting; then Leave the body ends it.
b4.i3: Design spell (with Sorcery) writes a new spell formula; its card has Learn it (Good Karma) and, in a group, Add to the group's grimoire. Create ally… makes an ally spirit by ritual (it counts for the familiar ordeal).

magic.b5: Changing the Astral choice (on the Main tab) to perceiving or projecting during your turn in combat spends an action; coming back to physical is free. While projecting, buttons for physical actions are greyed out.
magic.b6: A barrier spell or a ward becomes a Barrier actor (see Spells). Its sheet has its kind, the current and full rating, and Restore (back to full). Magicians and spirits on the astral plane push through with Force barrier; each net success lowers the current rating.
magic.b7: The rules for all of these are in your SR2 rulebook (and its magic supplements).

conjuring.title: Conjuring and spirits
conjuring.b1: Anyone with the Conjuring skill gets a Conjuring section (on a character's Magic tab) with Summon and Banish, and on a character True name… (bind a free spirit whose true name you know). The list shows your spirits with Force, services left and kind; click a name to open its sheet. A line under it counts your bound elementals against the most you may hold.
conjuring.b2: An elemental arrives after its ritual hours (see Under way). A Karma re-roll of a summoning after the spirit exists changes its services (a player's goes to the GM as an Apply (GM) card), but not if its services have changed since.
conjuring.b3: A summoned spirit is a Spirit actor. A player who can't create actors gets a Create spirit (GM) button on the card for the GM. The spirit's sheet has:

b4.i1: The top row: Kind, spirit type, the element (elementals) or domain (nature spirits; outside its domain warns when the scene's environment doesn't match), Great form, Services and Use a service. A nature spirit shows when it leaves (sunrise or sunset). Free spirits and allies have a True name (and free spirits Spirit energy).
b4.i2: The attributes: each is the Force plus the number in the Force + row.
b4.i3: Tick Materialized when physical attacks can reach it, and Immunity to normal weapons for its extra armor. Manifest shows while it is not materialized.
b4.i4: Its Attacks (with Astral attack and Force barrier), its powers and spells (cast with its Force).
b4.i5: Folded at the bottom: Effects, Powers, weaknesses and notes, and Adjustments (a Reaction bonus, extra initiative dice and the Combat Pool spent).
b4.i6: Dismiss deletes the spirit and its tokens. When you may not delete them yourself, the GM's browser does it, so a GM must be logged in.

conjuring.b5: An ally's sheet has an Ally section: its master buys abilities for Good Karma (Buy), teaches it a spell (Teach a spell…, Good Karma per Force) and, with the sense link, uses its senses (Master uses my senses).

spells.title: Spells
spells.b1: Each spell row shows its category, type, duration, the learned Force (a box), damage and drain. Cast opens the cast dialog: Force, target, and the Spell Pool split between casting and drain. The drain is rolled with the cast. The target gets a Resist button.
spells.b2: The cast dialog also has, where they apply: Anchor it instead (it waits in the Anchored list on the Magic tab until released), Cast as a ritual (it takes hours; team members and an astral spotter help, and the card's Send the spell casts it at the end), an elemental's aid (costs a service), sustaining with a free sustaining focus, a fetish in hand, and a ward the spell crosses.
spells.b3: A barrier spell or a ward (Ward… on the Magic tab) becomes a Barrier actor; when you can't create actors the card has Create it (GM) or Create ward (GM). Then Draw it on the map places its region (set the radius and click the map).
spells.b4: Row icons: pin, place the area on the map (area spells), cast at an object or wall (the cube, physical spells), learn at a higher Force for Good Karma (the up arrow), offer it to your group's grimoire (the book).
spells.b5: The + opens the Add window at Spells. Learning a spell with Karma rolls a learning test first (on by default) and may take time: see Under way.

powers.title: Powers
powers.b1: Powers belong to critters, spirits and anyone else who has one. The row says what the power does. Use rolls it; the target gets a Resist button. An allergy has an exposed tick box and a Contact button.
powers.b2: The pin puts a usable power at the top of the sheet. A critter that must feed shows when it last ate, with Feed. On Under spells and powers, the GM can remove an effect you can't end yourself (dispelled, cured).

matrix.title: Matrix
matrix.b1: The Matrix tab shows when the character owns a cyberdeck or a program.

b2.i1: Cyberdecks: tick In use on the deck you run. Build… builds a deck or upgrades a part (a test).
b2.i2: With a deck in use: the persona ratings, Sim and Connection, Hacking Pool, Matrix initiative, Detection Factor and memory.
b2.i3: Jack in, then Log on or Operation, Attack, Perceive, Maneuver, Medic (with the program) and Jack out. Once jacked in you travel with Log on; the GM has a Move button that goes straight to a host.
b2.i4: The host lists in Jack in and Operation show only the hosts your character has found; a host's code shows once it has been analyzed.
b2.i5: The Persona track is the Matrix condition monitor. Click a box to set it.
b2.i6: Programs: tick Loaded (loading while jacked in takes time). The buttons show where they apply: Run for Slow and Restore, Launch for a frame (in a host) or an agent (jacked in), Release for smoke in a host. Other utilities work through Operation, Attack and the rest. Write… writes a new program.
b2.i7: Frames and agents you launched: Operation and Attack (from their host), Search hosts… (an agent searches by itself), and the trash icon to recall one. Click a name for its sheet: what it carries, its Matrix track, Attack and Restore.
b2.i8: Downloaded data: the files in your deck.
b2.i9: A security decker of the host gets Security. An otaku sees their Channels (the + raises one for Karma) and Complex form… beside Write….
b2.i10: On a wireless connection, type the distance to the relay to check the signal. The section also lists LTG numbers you know (× forgets one), defenses loaded, maneuvers in force and who rides your hitcher jacks (others ride along with the Hitch quick button).

matrix.b3: Warnings (traced, held, crippled, a damaged deck, psychotropic IC effects, smoke, time on the way to a host) show in red with what you can do about them; the GM has an × or eraser to clear them. Gray IC damage to a deck is permanent: build the damaged part again to replace its chip (Repair works only under the GM's house rule).
matrix.b4: Cards from IC and jacking out carry the follow-up buttons: Resist dump shock, Deck damage, Resist biofeedback, a psychotropic Resist, Resist overload, and against black IC a second Resist for your icon. Jacking out without a Graceful Logoff risks dump shock, and psychotropic IC that hit you test your mind when you jack out. On an NPC sheet the Matrix is a section, not a tab.

rigging.title: Rigging
rigging.b1: The Rigging tab shows for a character with a control rig or a remote control deck, or at a vehicle's controls. It has the control rig rating, rigged initiative and the Control Pool (usable only while jumped in). On an NPC sheet it is a section, not a tab.

b2.i1: Take the controls…: pick a vehicle you own (the GM gives you ownership) and drive it by hand or jump in. Anyone else is put at the wheel with Driver… on the vehicle sheet. The vehicles and drones you bought or were given from the shop are listed here too.
b2.i2: At the controls: Driving test, Jump in or Jump out (keep driving), and Let go. The vehicle's Handling, Speed, Body, Armor and damage show. The Drive quick button rolls a driving test too.
b2.i3: Remote control deck: Subscribe a drone…, then Group driving test… and Group attack…. Each drone shows its Pilot, status, who controls it and its link; the × unsubscribes it.
b2.i4: Jumped into a site's security system: its devices, alert and tally, and Jump out.

rigging.b3: Jumping in needs a control rig, and a rigger adaptation on the vehicle (drones count as adapted; the rigger adaptation goes in on top of a remote adaptation, under Modifications on the vehicle sheet). Jumping in from outside the vehicle also needs a remote control deck, and a link that is not jammed or spoofed; out of range it warns, or stops you if the house rules say so. Without a control rig you can still drive by hand.
rigging.b4: Damage to a vehicle you are jumped into comes back on a card with Resist feedback (or Resist dump shock when it is destroyed or the link is cut).
rigging.b5: The Drone link quick button (on characters and NPCs, when there are vehicles) intercepts a drone's remote link or spoofs it a command. Intercepting needs a remote control deck or a radio (under the Unified Rules Revamp, a remote control deck, and an encrypted link is decrypted first). Spoofing needs a remote control deck. An intercepted link shows Link intercepted on the vehicle sheet until the GM clears it; with the house rule that lets a spoof take the drone over, a spoofed one shows Link spoofed. A character with a jammer has a Jam quick button.
rigging.b6: Vehicles and drones have their own sheet: see Vehicle sheets.

cyberware.title: Cyberware and bioware
cyberware.b1: Cyberware and bioware, each with an Installed tick box. Ticking it by hand skips the surgery: use it for ware fitted before play. Ware that isn't installed has a Surgery button: pick who operates, the care while recovering, and whether to pay for a hospital. Recovery shows under the list with the days left; the bed icon changes the care (the GM's × ends it). Damaged ware has Repair; the burst or wrench icon marks it damaged or repaired. An adrenal pump has Activate and Switch off.
cyberware.b2: Lines under the list show the Body Index and other notes, and a Rejection test button when over the limit.
cyberware.b3: A grade changes the Essence and the price. The item's Essence field keeps the standard cost; its sheet shows At this grade with the Essence and price the grade gives. Hover over the Essence line on the Main tab to see which ware makes up the loss.

gear.title: Gear
gear.b1: Everything else the character carries, with a quantity box (it works in Play mode too). Buttons appear by kind of gear: Take (drugs), Apply patch, Play (sim chips), Plant…, Listen and Sweep… (bugs), Radio check and Listen in… (radios), Check… (IDs), Expose… (toxins), Set charge (explosives), Repair… (broken gear). Chips have a Slotted tick box.
gear.b2: The cart icon looks for more of the item: a find test. Its card says how long finding it takes and has Buy for ¥… and Haggle (an opposed test against the seller that moves the price; its card has a new Buy button). With waiting on, what you buy arrives when the find time has passed (Under way). An item on the sheet that isn't in use (added as a wish list) leaves it until it arrives; one in use stays, and the bought copies arrive beside it. To sell an item, open it and click Fence… (see Item sheets).
gear.b3: Lines under the list warn about unlicensed gear (with the fines), list what a licence covers, and warn about carrying too much.
gear.b4: On an NPC sheet, Other gear holds its armor, cyberware and gear as chips.

itemSheet.title: Item sheets
itemSheet.b1: Click an item's name (or its pencil) to open its sheet. The sheet shows the fields for that kind of item, in sections. The chat icon in its header posts the item to chat.

b2.i1: Template: pick a generic or GM-saved template and click Fill in to copy its settings. The GM has Save as template, which puts the item in every Add window, and a trash icon that deletes the picked world template.
b2.i2: Weapons: the Kind list (firearm, melee, thrown and so on) shows only the fields for that kind. Show every field shows them all.
b2.i3: Cost and legality: cost, Availability, Street Index, Legality and, where it fits, a Permit tick box (the GM’s: players use Get a permit…, see the shop) and a Broken tick box; a warning says what carrying it without a permit risks. On a character's item with a cost: Find… (an Availability test; its card has Buy for ¥… and Haggle), Buy (pay now; a player character out of creation finds it first) and Fence… (sell it: a Negotiation test sets the offer, and the card has a Sell for ¥… button). With the GM's Heat house rule on, stolen goods have a Heat that lowers what a fence pays.
b2.i4: A magical site (library, circle, lodge) on a character has Raise… to build or raise it.
b2.i5: Spells, adept powers and cyberdecks have their own sections: a spell's casting, damage, drain and sustaining (and, folded, the effects it gives while it lasts); a power's cost, level and bonuses; a deck's persona ratings, memory and options. See Spells, Powers and Matrix.

itemSheet.b3: Hover a field for what it does. The rules behind the numbers are in your SR2 rulebook.
itemSheet.b4: Custom tweaks (every item) are for bespoke gear and modifications the rules don't cover. Press + and pick what it changes: an attribute, Reaction, initiative dice, a dice pool, a skill's dice or TN (type the skill's name), damage Power (this weapon, every melee or ranged attack, or every attack), armor, or a note only. Give it a label and an amount; untick On to keep it without it counting. Tweaks count while the item does: ware installed and working, armor worn, weapons and gear carried, foci bonded, powers active, programs loaded. The Effects tab lists those in force.
itemSheet.b5: Carried (weapons, armor, gear): see Weapons and armor. From the description (weapons): when a weapon arrives (the shop, the Catalogue, a new entry, a catalogue file, a drop) or its description is edited, the description is read for accessories: gas vents, a silencer or suppressor, a laser sight, a scope, a shock pad, a bipod or tripod, a gyro mount, a smartgun link, a quick-draw holster. Only fields still at their default are filled: a value set by hand is never changed, and "no silencer" or "sold separately" is skipped. Accessories with no field of their own (a folding stock, a sling…) become note tweaks. The line at the top says what was filled; Undo puts it back and stops those accessories being read again.

health.title: Addictions and diseases
health.b1: These show on the Gear tab when they apply.

b2.i1: Addictions: the drug, rating and type, whether addicted (and in withdrawal), days clean, or recent doses while not yet addicted. Kick the habit when you can try.
b2.i2: Diseases: progress toward recovery, a Treated tick box, Resist when a test is due and Spread….

health.b3: The GM can clear either with ×. A radiation dose shows as a line between them (the GM's × clears it).

money.title: Money, lifestyle and the ledger
money.b1: Nuyen is the cash. Typing in the box writes no ledger line; Earn / spend… changes it and writes one.

b2.i1: Pick the Lifestyle: its status shows the days paid or overdue, and a line under it says what it does (finding gear, resting at home, grace days when overdue). Pay… pays it by the month or, where the house rules allow, offers Buy outright (owned for good, never overdue).
b2.i2: A safehouse you own has its own sheet: Pay to build… and Pay upkeep… pay from your character; the GM sets it up.
b2.i3: Pick a DocWagon contract (when the GM's house rules use them): Pay… pays it by the year, and Call calls a team now. The biomonitor calls by itself when the wearer is dying.

money.b3: The Ledger lists the latest 15 changes to nuyen, Good Karma and the Karma Pool, with their reasons.

spendKarma.title: Karma and Spend Karma
spendKarma.b1: The Upkeep tab's Karma shows Good Karma (what you spend), Karma earned in all, and the Karma Pool. The GM awards Karma and nuyen.
spendKarma.b2: Spend Karma… opens the Spend Karma window. It also opens from the star on the Current tab and from the Creation tab.

b3.i1: Attributes and Skills: each row shows the rating now, the next step and the Karma. Click Raise. Specializations and concentrations have rows of their own. The + on Skills learns a new skill with the skill picker.
b3.i2: Spells (magicians): raise a spell's Force, or + to learn a new one in the Add window.
b3.i3: More: Initiate…, Gain an edge… and Buy off a flaw, where they apply.
b3.i4: Recent Karma: the last few Karma changes, in and out.

spendKarma.b4: A row you can't afford is dimmed with the reason. With the approval queue on, each spend becomes a request and shows under Waiting for the GM. If the GM turns the queue off, cancel a waiting request with × and spend again.
spendKarma.b5: Training time is on by default: the Karma goes at once and the rating rises when the training is done (Under way). Learning tests are on by default too: raising or learning a spell rolls a learning test first, and the Karma is paid only on success. Costs follow your SR2 rulebook and the GM's house rules.
spendKarma.b6: After creation, raises normally go through Spend Karma, but ratings stay editable by hand: a raise typed in is kept, with a note that no Karma was spent. While the GM runs the approval queue, the lock comes back and typed raises are refused. (A house rule keeps the lock on all the time.)

underWay.title: Under way: things that take time
underWay.b1: Some things take game time. Depending on the GM's house rules: training a raised attribute or skill, learning or designing spells and other magical work, repairs, writing programs and building deck parts, vehicle work, and gear you buy: found in the shop or with a find card, it arrives when the time it took to find has passed; bought with Buy now, after its Availability time. Items with no Availability arrive at once.
underWay.b2: While they wait they are listed under Under way on the Upkeep tab (and on the Current tab), with the time left and what was paid.

b3.i1: Instructor… (training only): an instructor's test shortens the time.
b3.i2: The × gives it up. What was paid comes back.
b3.i3: The GM sees two more icons: the hourglass changes the time left, and fast-forward finishes it now.

underWay.b4: Things finish when the GM moves game time on. On the GM panel, the Party tab lists everyone's things under way, and the Requests tab the open orders.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.b1: The + adds a contact: name, level, who they are, Loyalty, what they know, a fee per legwork, their own dice for digging, favours, notes and whether they are a fixer. Each row shows these. Click the name to edit. The handshake + and − count favours owed either way.
contacts.b2: In Shadowrun, Mr. Johnson is the name runners give whoever hires them for a job: usually a corporate go-between who never gives a real name, so every employer is "Mr. Johnson" (or "Ms. Johnson"). A contact can be one; they pay for the job and know about it, which makes their legwork easier.
contacts.b3: Legwork… asks around through that contact. Say what about and pick how hard it is to find out (TN 2 for general information up to 14 for top secret). Tick it if it's the contact's specialty, or if the contact is a fixer or a Mr. Johnson (easier), or if you go through a friend of a friend (harder). A buddy or a friend for life adds dice. You can also pay extra for more dice (up to the contact's Loyalty), let the contact dig with their own dice, or Call in a favour for extra dice and no fee (if they owe you none, you owe them one). The card says what you learn.
contacts.b4: Finding things through a contact: when you find something (Find & buy in the shop, Find… or Buy on an item), a character with contacts is asked how. On your own is the usual find. Helped by a contact works as legwork: a buddy or a friend for life adds dice, you can pay for more dice (up to their Loyalty) or call in a favour, a contact with dice of their own looks too (the better result counts), and their fee is paid now; a restricted or forbidden item is easier to find than openly (by default half the legality TN). A contact ticked as a fixer can also find it for you: the fixer rolls their own dice (or two per level), legality doesn't count, but the price includes their cut (by default 10%), it takes half as long again, and there is no Haggle. A favour adds dice and waives the fee or the cut. The GM sets these numbers, or turns it off, in the house rules (Time to get things).

adding.title: The shop (the Add window)
adding.b1: The Shop button opens it as the shop: only the tabs that sell things (weapons, armor, gear, ware, foci, programs, decks, vehicles, kits), ready to buy. It is in the SR2e tools window, the SR2e group of the left toolbar, and the title bar of your character sheet (the GM: for the selected token). The + on a heading (Weapons, Armor, Spells, Cyberware, Gear and so on) opens the same window with every tab, at that kind of item.

b2.i1: Tick the categories above the list to show only those (Melee, Pistols, SMGs, Rifles…; Headware, Bioware…; none ticked shows everything); the list is sorted by category, then name. Search it, tick the rows you want and set the amount: quantity, rating, Force or level.
b2.i2: Pay: Free (creation, GM gift, loot), Find & buy or Buy now (nuyen), or Learn with Good Karma (skills and spells). Out of creation a player character buys by finding: Find & buy. The GM, NPCs and characters in the creation wizard have Buy now (the GM can give everyone Buy now again in the house rules).
b2.i3: Find ticked gives each ticked row its own find card: Etiquette (or Charisma) against its Availability TN, with the lifestyle and Street Cred; the Karma Pool works on it. The card says how long finding it took and has Buy for ¥… and Haggle. With contacts, you are first asked whether to look on your own or through one of them (see Contacts). Buying pays then; with waiting on, the item arrives when that time has passed (Under way).
b2.i4: Not found: you can try again once its base time has passed in game time. The row shows the wait (the GM can drop the wait in the house rules).
b2.i5: Add ticked adds them (Free, Buy now, Learn). Buying or learning posts a chat line. A player's free add is whispered to the GM.
b2.i6: Armor, ware, foci, programs and kits have an Arrives… tick box (worn, installed, bonded, loaded, ready to use). It starts ticked for Free and unticked for Buy now (a magician's focus in creation arrives bonded). Unticked, the item arrives needing that step: bought cyberware needs Surgery on the Gear tab. Things found and bought arrive the same way.
b2.i7: Some rows keep their listed rating when bought: change it on the sheet afterwards, or add the item free.
b2.i8: The Blank button makes an empty item and opens its sheet.
b2.i9: When the GM has made starter kits, a Kits tab offers them: a bundle of items in one go (found line by line with Find & buy).

adding.b3: The list holds the system's generic templates (Template in the From column: plain classes such as "Heavy pistol", no rulebook data), the GM's own templates, world items and compendium items; the GM may show players less (below). A kind with no entries means the GM hasn't made any yet. The Price column counts the item's Street Index (hover it to see the index), and the Legal column shows its legality.
adding.b4: For the GM: Configure Settings has Shop: what players see (everything, only your catalogue and kits, or only what you mark) and Shop: forbidden things on sale (off hides Forbidden items from players). On the buying tabs you see a Shop column: tick your templates and world items to put them in the shop; the mark travels with catalogue files. The GM panel's Requests tab lists the Open orders.
adding.b5: The Skills tab has Open the skill picker (see The skill picker).
adding.b6: Vehicles and drones are on their own tab: the GM’s catalogue vehicles (the Catalogue (SR2e) actor folder, or any vehicle the GM marks In the shop) and vehicle compendiums. Find and buy one as anything else; it is a new actor of your own, made by the GM’s client (so the GM must be logged in), in the Owned vehicles folder, and it arrives when the time to get it has passed (only the GM can cancel a vehicle order). A vehicle with no price set can’t be bought by players: the GM sets its Cost on the vehicle sheet (or gives it free).
adding.b7: Legality: hover the Legal column for what it means. Found openly, a Restricted item is harder to find (by default TN +2), and a Forbidden one (when the GM sells them) harder and slower (TN +4, time ×2); the find card says what carrying it without a permit risks. A Needs a permit or Restricted item can have a permit: Get a permit… on its item sheet (or a vehicle’s sheet) pays a share of its cost (by default 10%, at least ¥100; restricted 25%, at least ¥500) and the permit comes through after 7 days (restricted 30) of game time (Under way); with the approval queue on it goes to the GM first. The Permit box is then the GM’s to tick. The GM sets these numbers, or puts the old ways back, in the house rules (Time to get things).

creationWizard.title: The creation wizard
creationWizard.b1: On a new character, the Creation tab (and the Bio tab) has Create character…. It opens the wizard. The steps run along the top: Priorities, Metatype, Attributes, Magic, Skills, Resources, Contacts, Finish. Back and Next move between them; click a step to jump to it. A ✓ or ⚠ on a step shows whether its checks are met.

b2.i1: Priorities: pick a letter, A to E, for each of Race, Magic, Attributes, Skills and Resources. Picking a letter another one holds swaps the two.
b2.i2: Metatype: choices the Race priority doesn't allow are greyed out.
b2.i3: Attributes: base ratings, with points used and allowed.
b2.i4: Magic: mundane, full magician, adept or aspected, as the priority allows; tradition and totem; spells or adept powers through the Add window. A magician's foci bought in creation arrive bonded and count against the spell points.
b2.i5: Skills: the + for each kind opens the skill picker (free in creation). Set ratings and specializations here; a specialization taken here lowers the skill as the trade works, and a check flags a trade that doesn't. Common skills you haven't taken are listed: click one to add it at 1.
b2.i6: Resources: the lifestyle, months paid ahead or bought outright, and the Shopping buttons, which open the Add window. Free and bought items both come out of the Resources nuyen.
b2.i7: Contacts: Add a contact, then its name, level (1 to 3) and role. The first ones are free; more cost nuyen.
b2.i8: Finish: every build check with ✓ or ✗; click a check to go to its step. You can finish with checks unmet; the record notes it. Finishing pays the lifestyle and keeps the cash left, as the hint says.

creationWizard.b3: The Totals panel keeps the build checks in view at every step. Closing the wizard keeps the draft: Continue creation… opens it again. Finish creation freezes the creation record.
creationWizard.b4: For a character made another way, Record as it stands freezes it as it is. Quick build… on the Bio tab is the older builder that reads typed lists. Import a stat block… on the Bio tab fills the sheet from a pasted character write-up, with a preview of what it read; the GM can record the result as the creation. The priority table's values come from your SR2 rulebook and the GM's house rules.
creationWizard.b5: With the approval queue on, a character who has earned Karma can't start the wizard or be recorded by a player: the GM does it.
creationWizard.b6: The wizard advises and never refuses: a metatype or magic the priorities don't pay for, an attribute above the creation maximum, or gear over the Resources budget are allowed, and the totals mark them. Finish creation still says what isn't met. (The GM's house rule can bring back the greyed-out choices and limits.)

creationRecord.title: Creation record and advancement log
creationRecord.b1: After Finish, the Creation tab shows the record: the build, attributes, skills, spells, adept powers, ware, gear, contacts, edges and flaws, and the folded Build checks at the finish (click to open).
creationRecord.b2: The Advancement log lists every gain since: Karma in, raises, purchases and approvals, with who and when. A line above it adds them up.
creationRecord.b3: Once a character has a record (or, with the approval queue on, once they are out of the wizard), a player raises ratings through Spend Karma. Typing a higher rating, Force or level is refused; lowering is allowed. Essence can't be typed at all. With the queue on, typing more nuyen or Karma is refused too: the GM awards them. The GM can type anything.
creationRecord.b4: The GM also has Log note… (write a line), a trash icon on each line (only the log changes) and Reopen creation (throws the record away and opens the wizard again; the log stays).

approval.title: The approval queue
approval.b1: The GM can turn on the approval queue in Configure Settings: Players' purchases and Karma wait for the GM. It is off by default. When it is on, a player who buys, adds or learns something, or spends Karma, sends a request instead. This applies to every character that isn't in the creation wizard, including one with no creation record yet. Building a character in the wizard doesn't wait.
approval.b2: With the queue on, a player records only spending with Earn / spend… (the GM records nuyen coming in), and copying an item with the copy icon becomes a free-add request, and so does adding, changing or deleting an edge or flaw by hand. Buy on a find card sends the purchase, with its price and the time it takes to arrive, and that card's Buy is then spent. Asking for the same thing twice replaces the older request.
approval.b3: Players see their requests under Waiting for the GM on the Creation tab and in Spend Karma, and can cancel one with ×.
approval.b4: The GM gets a notification. The GM panel's Requests tab, with a count, lists them: who filed it, what will run and the cost (not enough now when the character can't pay).

b5.i1: Approve first shows what will really run, read from the request itself, with its cost and who filed it. A player can change a request after filing it, so check it.
