A name marked (filer not verified) wasn't seen filing it this session. If the request no longer checks out, the confirm says it won't run: decline it.
b5.i2: Confirming runs it at once and pays from the character. If it fails (not enough Karma or nuyen, a failed learning test), the request closes and the player is told.
b5.i3: Decline takes an optional reason and whispers it to the player.

approval.b6: For the GM: the queue is a table rule, not a lock. Every check runs in the player's browser, so a player who knows how can skip it. The Requests tab and the advancement log show what was done.

bio.title: Bio: edges, reputation and notes

b1.i1: Edges and flaws (when the GM's house rules use them): the + adds one with no Karma, for creation; its name changes it and the trash deletes it. The star gains an edge in play for Good Karma. The coin buys a flaw off. After creation, with the GM's approval queue on, adding, changing or deleting one by hand becomes a request to the GM (see The approval queue).
b1.i2: Reputation (when the GM's house rules use it): Street Cred, Notoriety and Public Awareness. Street Cred may be worked out from career Karma, and then can't be typed. The GM has a Recognised? button.
b1.i3: Biography and Notes: rich text. Open the editor to write; inline tests work here too (Inline tests).

bio.b2: Before the character has a creation record, the Bio tab also has Create character…, Quick build… and Import a stat block… (see The creation wizard).

tokenArt.title: Pictures and tokens
tokenArt.b1: Every new actor gets a picture and token of the system's own (unless it already has one): people a portrait by metatype and figure, with a small badge for their archetype and a rim in its colour; critters, spirits, vehicles and drones, IC, hosts, barriers, sites and safehouses a picture of their own kind. The art is the system's own, drawn by an AI (Anthropic's Claude) for it; see Credits and licence.

b2.i1: Picture and token (a character's Bio tab; an NPC sheet's folded section): Figure picks the masculine or feminine portrait (a new character gets one from its name), and Archetype the badge. Automatic works it out: a mage or shaman from the tradition, an adept, a rigger from a control rig, a decker from a cyberdeck, a street samurai from wired or boosted reflexes or cyberweapons, a face from a high Charisma; a generated NPC keeps the generator's role. None shows the portrait without a badge.
b2.i2: While the picture is the default art the system gave, it follows these choices (on the GM's screen, which also updates the actor's linked tokens on the map), the metatype, a vehicle's category or a spirit's kind by itself. A picture you set by hand (even one of the system's art files, or one found by name, see Your look) is never replaced; Use the default art puts the default back on the picture, the token and linked tokens on the map (asking first).
b2.i3: Only the actor's own picture and token change, and linked tokens already on the map. Tokens of unlinked NPCs placed earlier keep the picture they had.
b2.i4: Default token art (GM panel, Setup tab): how many actors still show Foundry's stand-in, and a button to give them all the default art. The world setting Default token art (Configure Settings, SR2e) turns it off: new actors keep Foundry's stand-in, and the default art already given no longer follows changes.

tokenArt.b3: What the rim colour means. The rim says what kind of thing a token is, in the same colours as the sheets' tabs and the strips on chat cards (the Street theme's shades; the other themes use lighter or darker shades of the same colours). The colours are chosen to stay apart with each kind of colour blindness, and the badge and the picture tell them apart as well:

b4.i1: Red, combat: street samurai, mercenaries and gangers.
b4.i2: Violet, magic: mages, shamans, physical adepts and talismongers; every spirit (an elemental shows its element in the picture) and magical barriers.
b4.i3: Green, the Matrix: deckers, hosts and IC (white, gray and black IC differ by the picture).
b4.i4: Orange, rigging: riggers and technicians, and every vehicle and drone.
b4.i5: Gold, the street: faces, corporate suits and fixers, and safehouses.
b4.i7: Blue, security: security guards and secured sites.
b4.i8: Steel grey: a person without an archetype badge. Tan grey: a critter (an Awakened one also glows violet).

npcSheets.title: NPC sheets
npcSheets.b1: NPCs use a compact sheet: the attributes in a grid (click a short name to roll), PR (Professional Rating), Grunts (the group size) and how many are down, Threat (Threat Rating), Metatype (untick Add racial modifiers if the ratings already include them), the summary bar and status strip, the condition monitor with Resist Damage and Hazard, and Skills, Weapons, Spells, Powers and Other gear. The NPC generator fills in PR and Threat (and a Karma Pool when the house rules give NPCs one); on a hand-made NPC you type them. The layout choice works here too.

b2.i1: Import: paste a stat block. It overwrites the attributes and updates items with the same name. What it can't read is reported; an Essence or power cost the block leaves out is guessed, and you are told which.
b2.i2: Split (GM): one unlinked token per standing grunt, beside this one. Morale and group attacks then count the tokens.
b2.i3: A magically active NPC has the Astral choice, a Magic section and Conjuring like a character's (see Magic); a decker or rigger has the Matrix and Rigging sections. On an NPC these are sections, not tabs.
b2.i4: Folded at the bottom: Effects, Powers, weaknesses and notes, Critter (Essence drained or gained, Regenerate, a shapeshifter's Form and Shift form) and Adjustments (base Essence, natural Magic, vision, Reaction and initiative bonuses, the Karma Pool and Combat Pool spent; the rotate icon beside Init refreshes the Karma Pool).

vehicles.title: Vehicle sheets
vehicles.b1: A vehicle or drone sheet has its ratings (Handling, Speed, Accel, Body, Armor, Signature, Autonav, Pilot, Sensor, ECM, ECCM, ECD, off-road Handling, Object resistance), damaged systems (tick tires, sensors or engine when shot out), autosofts (they help its own autopilot), seating and the Damage track (click a box to set it). Category and Skill choose the driving skill; tick Drone for a drone. Design… builds it from a chassis and a powerplant. Under Cost and legality the GM sets what it costs in the shop: its cost, Availability, Street Index and legality. A vehicle that needs a permit has Get a permit… (paid by the character who bought it, or your own).

b2.i1: Control: who drives it (Driver… puts someone at the wheel, by hand or jumped in; Autopilot hands it back), the current speed and off-road, Handling now and crash Power. When the speed is limited, Push… changes it by more than the Accel. Buttons: Driving test, Crash test, Crash, Repair test… and Reset (GM: clears all damage).
b2.i2: Weapons: mounted weapons; the + adds them and Fire shoots one (pick who fires: the driver, a gunner aboard, a security rigger or the autopilot). Ram… rams a target; the defense card then has Rammer's damage. With Firmpoints and Hardpoints set in the ratings, a line under the heading counts the points used and warns when a weapon doesn't fit. A weapon's item sheet has a Point choice for the mount it takes.
b2.i3: Sensors: active or passive Mode, low-light and thermographic sensors, Sensor test… (a success locks on: the lock shows as a chip, × drops it), and Jam… with the vehicle's ECM. A jammed link shows in red with an × to clear it.
b2.i4: Modifications: Add one, then Install… (a mechanic's test that takes time and charges the cost) or Take out. Work on a vehicle your players don't own finishes on a GM card.
b2.i5: Cargo: the + loads gear. With Load (kg) or Cargo Factor set, the sheet counts what it carries and warns when overloaded.
b2.i6: Chase: Give chase…, then the gap in metres, Chase turn and End chase. A won maneuver shows its TN bonus for the Combat Turn.
b2.i7: Aboard: Put someone aboard; the × takes them off.

vehicles.b3: A drone's Link encryption guards its remote link against Drone link. Guided missiles fired at a vehicle lock on to its Signature, and sensor locks run out after a few Combat Turns without a new sensor test.

printing.title: Printing a sheet and reporting a bug
printing.b1: Print a sheet. The Print button (a printer) in the title bar of a character, NPC or spirit sheet opens a small window: tick Empty condition monitor for a sheet to fill in at the table, or Leave out the biography and notes. Then:

b2.i1: Print opens your browser's print dialog. Choose a printer, or Save as PDF to keep a file.
b2.i2: Open as a page shows the sheet in a new browser tab, to print or save from there. If nothing opens, allow pop-ups for your Foundry address.
b2.i3: Save as a file downloads the sheet as a web page (.html): open it in any browser and print it from there. Use it when neither of the others works (some desktop-app setups).

printing.b3: If you own the character, a third box, Include the notes' secret sections, puts the secret parts of the notes on the paper too; they are left out otherwise (so a GM can print an NPC to hand out).
printing.b4: The printout is black on white with thin lines, so it uses little ink: the name, attributes, derived values and pools, the condition monitor (filled boxes are grey with a slash), then skills, weapons, armor, cyberware and bioware, spells, powers, foci, Matrix gear, gear, contacts, edges and flaws, and the notes. Empty lists are left out. You can print any sheet you can see.
printing.b5: Report a bug. The Report a bug button at the top of this guide's topic list (also in Configure Settings, under the system's settings) opens a text ready to paste into a new issue on the project's GitHub page. It holds the system and Foundry versions, your browser, your active modules, the rules source, the house rules your GM changed and the system's recent errors in this browser. Press Copy, paste it into the issue and describe what happened. Nothing is sent anywhere by itself. Read it before posting: error messages can name things in your world. (Configure Settings: Keep recent errors for bug reports turns the error log off in your browser.)

gmPanel.title: The GM panel
gmPanel.b1: Open it with Alt+G, the GM panel button in the Actors sidebar or the SR2e tools window. Tabs: Scene, Combat, Party, NPCs, World, Tools, Log, Requests, Setup. The Undo button sits just under them.
gmPanel.b2: On sheets and chat cards, parts meant for the GM (buttons marked (GM) and the GM: row on cards) have a striped amber edge (a striped underline on small buttons). A player may see one on a sheet, but the system refuses it if they click it.
gmPanel.b3: The Scene tab works on the scene you are viewing:

b4.i1: Scene: background count, weather, terrain, darkness, environment tags and background count sources.
b4.i2: Regions with an SR2e environment: draw a Region on the map, open its config and fill in SR2e environment: background count (aspected, toxic), environment tags, weather, light, smoke, a ward or barrier whose edge it is, or a camera or sensor that watches it. Tokens inside are affected by themselves. The list shows each region and who is inside; click a name to open its config.
b4.i3: A ward's edge stops astral forms (Configure Settings, Ward regions stop astral forms: stop, warn or off; your own moves only warn). When someone walks into a watched region you get a whispered card with Detection test, or the test is rolled at once (Camera and sensor regions). Hidden tokens, the site's guards, and devices that are off or bypassed don't set it off; only an astral sensor sees astral forms.
b4.i4: Presets: save this scene's conditions (the disk icon: background count and sources, tags, weather, terrain, and darkness if ticked) and put them on the scene you are viewing (the play icon); the trash can deletes one.
b4.i6: Encounter notes: one set per scene. Players don't see them on screen, but a player could read them from the browser console: keep real secrets in a GM-only journal.
b4.i7: Charges on a timer: set one off now, a disarm test (select the token of whoever disarms it: Demolitions against the TN shown), or take it away with no test.
b4.i8: Fires (start one at the selected token, spread every fire one Combat Turn, put one out, pick a fuel and mark selected drawings as fuel) and Damaged walls (repair fully, or a Build/Repair test).
b4.i9: Walls: a wall's own config window has SR2 barrier rating (added to the target's armor when shot through it, and taken off a blast's Power; left blank, gunfire counts the default rating and a blast is stopped completely), SR2: burns (a fire burns through it) and SR2: security door (a door breaks at half its rating, a security door only at 0).

gmTime.title: Time
gmTime.b1: The Scene tab's Time shows the world time (and the Combat Turn in a fight) and buttons from +3 s (one Combat Turn) to +1 year. A week or more asks first (house rules, GM tools: the days in a month and a year, and when to ask). Moving time on is what finishes things under way and runs other timers (drugs, diseases, recovery, rent, fires). Undo moves the time back.
gmTime.b2: The Party tab lists everyone's things under way, each with Change the time left (hourglass) and Finish it now (fast-forward). The same icons show on the character's Upkeep tab for the GM.
gmTime.b3: What waits at all is set in the house rules, section Time to get things: the main switch, each area (magic, buying gear, repairs, Matrix work, vehicles), the Availability time multiplier for buying straight from the Add window, and the shortest wait. Training time for raised ratings is the Characters house rule about raising a skill or attribute. See House rules.
gmTime.b4: A calendar module, or the clock moved by hand: when world time jumps a week or more outside combat (a calendar setting the date when you turn it on, or you set the campaign's date), you are asked: Count it as time passed runs everything timed for it, as above; Only the date changes the date but not the characters' time, so drugs, recovery, upkeep and training keep the time they had left (the time of day stays the calendar's). Putting the date back the same way undoes it. The size of a big jump, or always counting, is a house rule (GM tools). The Scene tab's own buttons always count.

gmCombat.title: Combat and NPCs tabs
gmCombat.b1: Combat tab: the Combat Turn and pass, Start, back one turn, Next, Roll NPCs and Add selected. Each row has the crosshair (show and select the token), the token's initiative, ± buttons for Physical and Stun boxes, and quick icons: attack (target a token first), cast, defend, perceive, morale, roll initiative again.
gmCombat.b2: NPCs tab: Group roll… (one test, one card), Damage several… and Heal several… each ask who: the selected tokens, every NPC token on the scene, or the party. Group for morale and Ungroup work on the selected tokens; each morale group is then listed with a flag (its morale test) and an × (break it up). On this scene lists the tokens no player owns (up to 40) with the same quick icons.
gmCombat.b3: On both tabs, NPC rows show as compact stat cards (attributes, armor, initiative, weapon and damage). The card icon beside the heading switches to plain rows and back; the panel remembers.
gmCombat.b4: Foundry's combat tracker gets a banner with the Combat Turn, the pass, who is acting and how many are on full defense or delaying. The acting row is highlighted, delaying combatants are listed last under Delaying, and full defense shows as a badge. IC, frames and agents get an act button there.
gmCombat.b5: The tracker's header has Surprise test (every combatant rolls; hover it for how the result is used) and, when Foundry's own button isn't there, Roll NPCs. Rows you own have Delay, Act now or Done, a shield to declare full defense (out of turn it costs initiative), and a line with the pools left.

gmParty.title: Party tab
gmParty.b1: Party shows a card for each player character: portrait, name (opens the sheet), player, a small monitor with − / + for Physical and Stun boxes, wound TN and state, initiative in combat (the acting one is highlighted), pools, Good Karma and nuyen, and icons to open the sheet, show the token and roll initiative again. Buttons: Refresh pools (the party and everyone in the running combat), Refresh Karma Pools, Award Karma / nuyen (also in the Actors sidebar) and Heal several…. Karma Pools can also refresh by themselves at each new session or when a combat ends (house rules, Tests and dice: Karma Pools refresh on their own).
gmParty.b2: Money and Karma shows each character's nuyen, Good Karma, Karma Pool, career Karma and lifestyle, with the party's totals, and warns when rent is due within a week. Under way lists their things that take time.

gmTools.title: Tools tab: NPC generator and calculator

b1.i1: Open the NPC generator (also a button in the Actors sidebar): choose what to generate (a person, a group, an organisation, a contact, a spirit, a critter, a fixer's job, street names), a Threat Level from 0 to 5 and the options for that kind. People can arrive as tokens on the viewed scene, hidden from the players, and a group can be grouped for morale.
b1.i2: The Preview shows the result first; the line beside the buttons says what Create will do. Re-roll rolls again, and Post to GM whispers the preview. Create makes the actors in a Generated (SR2e) folder; an organisation or a job becomes a GM journal entry (plus its people if ticked), street names are posted to the GMs, and a contact can go straight onto a character's Contacts.
b1.i3: Dice and TN calculator: dice, base TN and modifiers (one per line, like Smoke +4) give the TN, each die's chance, the successes to expect, the chance of a disaster and of at least 1, 2, 3… successes. Roll it posts a card with your label, to the players too if you tick that.

gmSetup.title: Setup tab: players, tokens, kits and the catalogue

b1.i1: Starter demo: Create the demo makes a small world to try the system in: four runners (a street samurai, a mage, a decker and a rigger, as full characters), a gang, a corporate host with its security sheaf, a secured building (a maglocked door, a camera, an alarm), the runners' safehouse, the rigger's car and drone, a night scene with walls, a door and lamps, and the journal SR2e demo: try this, whose pages walk through a fight, a spell, the Matrix, rigging and a chase, security, and printing. It is the same in every world (the generators with a fixed seed), and everything goes in folders named "Demo (SR2e)". Give the runners to your players under Players and characters. Remove the demo (it asks first) deletes everything the demo made, wherever you moved it, the combats on its scene and demo tokens you placed on other scenes. Copies you made of demo documents (duplicated or imported) stay. A player given the rigger also needs to own the demo's vehicle and drone (Configure Ownership).
b1.i2: Rules source: Play with SR2E Book Rules or the SR2E Unified Rules Revamp (see the Unified Rules Revamp). It asks first, then changes the rules for everyone at once; your house rules still win.
b1.i3: Session checklist: lines for the start and the end of a session. Tick them as you go; a button on a line does that step. + adds a line; the circular arrow starts a new session and clears the ticks.
b1.i4: Players and characters: pick the character each player plays, then Save who plays whom. The player becomes its owner. Award to several… gives Karma and nuyen.
b1.i5: Token setup: linked tokens, Physical and Stun bars, vision from eyes and cyberware, who sees names and bars, disposition, and whether tokens already on scenes change too (Relink unlinked ones drops those tokens' own changes). Apply it to The party's tokens or Pick actors….
b1.i6: Portraits by name: with a Portrait folder set in Configure Settings (see Your look), Find portraits for every actor gives each actor that still has the default picture the one named after it.
b1.i7: Starter kits: bundles of items. Make one from a sheet (+) or empty (the box), drop items on it, edit it (pencil), and give it to actors (the gift): it asks whether things arrive ready to use (installed, worn, bonded). Players find kits on the Add window's Kits tab.
b1.i8: Item catalogue: the world's item templates, which show first in every Add window. Paste spreadsheet rows…, Export as CSV, Manage templates…, save or load a catalogue file, and templates to or from a compendium. A catalogue file holds templates and kits (to take to another world) and can also hold vehicles and drones, NPCs, critters and spirits, so one file can bring a whole data set into a world. Load a catalogue file… shows what the file has and asks first. New actors go in the folder Catalogue (SR2e), sorted into subfolders (vehicles and drones by kind, spirits, critters, NPCs; actors left at the top of the folder by an earlier load are sorted too, and anything you moved elsewhere stays put); an actor already in the world with the same name is never replaced. With Fill in missing values ticked, items already in the world with the same type and name (on characters too, and on actors the file also has) get the file's descriptive values (cost, Availability, a damage code, ranges, Essence…) only where theirs are still empty or zero. A value someone set is kept, and ratings, quantities, ammo, accessories and on/off switches are never changed. An actor already in the world is never changed itself. Any item sheet also has Save as template.
b1.i9: Characters from a stat block: paste a character write-up to make a new character.
b1.i10: Modules: which helpful modules are on, a tour of the GM panel, and a link to this guide.

gmWorld.title: World tab, hosts, sites and safehouses
gmWorld.b1: The World tab lists Magical groups (new, edit, a broken stricture, the grimoire), Matrix hosts (tally, alert to pick, reset, clear smoke), Building security sites (tally, alert to pick) and Safehouses with upkeep.

b2.i1: A host sheet has its node kind, the grid it is on and an LTG number to dial, the security code and value, the subsystems, the tally and alert (Reset tally; each intruder's own tally is listed), a shutdown in progress (Dump now) and the valid passcodes (× takes one away). It holds the Security sheaf (Generate sheaf rolls one for the host's code and value, replacing the steps; hosts the NPC generator makes come with one), IC (Launch IC), Data stores (Add file, Generate paydata, Reset found), the deckers inside, security deckers, subsystem data bombs and, on an LTG, comcalls.
b2.i2: An IC sheet sets its type, category, rating, damage, behavior (what it guards, what a trace does, a psychotropic payload), a Party name (IC with the same party act together: Party attack), construct behaviors and its host. Buttons: Attack (or Act), Locate (find a decker who broke contact) and Restore.
b2.i3: A site sheet has its alert, security tally (with the next step and Reset) and who responds, and how many Combat Turns or minutes after an alert they arrive. Devices: Add device, then per row link the selected token (where a camera sees from) or door wall (what a lock holds), switch it on or off, mark it bypassed, smash it, and Scan…, Detect… or Bypass…. Guards: select their tokens and press +, then Guards look…. Also Security steps (Add step), the Security rigger (Security rigger…, Jump out), Turrets and drones (vehicle actors with a mounted weapon; a Fire button per weapon) and a linked Matrix host: the site and the host raise each other's alerts, and a lockdown locks every linked door that isn't bypassed.
b2.i4: A safehouse sheet totals its cost, upkeep, space, comfort, security and the rest. Pay to build… and Pay upkeep… pay from a character you own; it can make the matching security site, ward and home host actors, and give a magician its library or lodge. People lists owners and residents, and Build it adds options by category. The GM also has Search for it… (someone looking for it) and the amount paid towards building, under the notes.

gmWorld.b3: Hover a button for what it does. The rules behind them are in your SR2 rulebook and its supplements.

gmUndo.title: Undo and recent rolls
gmUndo.b1: The Undo button just under the GM panel's tabs takes back the newest step, whoever made it. Ctrl+Shift+Z does the same. Ctrl+Z takes back whichever came last: a canvas edit on the layer you are on, or your own newest logged step (a player's steps are undone from the panel).
gmUndo.b2: The Log tab lists the steps, newest first. Each is one person's burst of changes; open it to see the lines. to here undoes every step down to that one. The log keeps the last 50 steps by default (house rules, GM tools); a step marked partly grew too big and can only be partly undone. The broom forgets the log (it changes nothing in the world). What undo can't do lists the limits. Changes are logged only while a GM has the world open in that browser.
gmUndo.b3: Recent rolls: click one to show its card in the chat log.

gmCards.title: Chat cards for the GM

b1.i1: Right-click a roll card and choose Change target number… to score it again with another base TN or other modifiers (a checklist of the modifiers that kind of test can take). Cards that already followed from it are not changed; the card says so.
b1.i2: On a player's card, a TN change and any button you click that runs their test again (a Karma re-roll, Avoid disaster, Buy a success, Use again, Send the spell, Learn it, Add to … grimoire, Detonate, It goes off, … throws it back) runs with that player's rights. What they don't own gets an Apply (GM) card, as their own click would, and any other change is stopped with a Not changed warning. Meanwhile, anything else your browser does with GM rights waits its turn. If something waits over 15 seconds you are warned: reload the window if nothing happens.
b1.i3: A damage resistance card has Undo (the condition monitor goes back) and −1 / +1 box buttons, in a GM: row with the striped edge.
b1.i4: Defending a second time against the same attack asks first (Already defended); so does resisting a card again (Already resisted, for example after Undo).
b1.i5: A spoofed or intercepted drone link shows on the vehicle sheet with an × to clear it. A player's intercept or takeover of a drone they don't own comes to you as an Apply (GM) card.
b1.i6: A card with several targets has Resist all…: tick who resists now (no pool dice). Targets who are done, or whose player is logged in, start unticked.
b1.i7: A damage card has Apply unresisted (full damage, no test or armor). A blast, or a shot fired through a wall, has Barriers… (damage the walls) instead.
b1.i8: Other buttons marked (GM) finish what a player's test started, for example Create it (GM) and Create ward (GM) after a summoning or a ward, Start the fire (GM), Team arrives (GM) for DocWagon, The deed is done (GM), Combine with the last blast (GM), Apply to the wall (GM) and Add it (GM) for a grimoire. A Detonate for a charge that is no longer on record (its explosive is gone, or the card is old) goes off only after you confirm its Power.

gmCards.b2: Apply (GM) and the security model. Players are not trusted: anyone can post a chat card that looks like a system card, with any data.

b3.i1: Apply (GM) buttons make changes a player's test asked for. On a card you posted, or one whose author owns what changes, the click applies at once. Otherwise a confirm lists exactly what will change, read from the card's data, and names who posted it. A card whose data isn't what the system posts, or whose author owns none of the characters it comes from, is refused (not applied).
b3.i2: Read every confirm before saying Yes. Go ahead only if it matches what happened at the table. Players get the same question (A card from another player) when another player's card would act for their character, except for ordinary tests such as Defend and Resist. You get it too when a player's card acts for one of your NPCs in a way that lasts (cyberware damage, a disease, a crash and so on).
b3.i3: Configure Settings, section Other: Apply players' GM-only changes by themselves (off by default). Even when it is on, it applies only a jam, a hold, a sensor lock or boxes on something the card's author owns. The system posts Apply (GM) cards only for what the author doesn't own, so in practice almost every card still waits for your click. Each change it does make is listed in a whispered note.
b3.i4: Section Rolls, dice and chat: NPCs resist damage by themselves (off by default). Your browser rolls damage and spell resistance, with no pool dice, for characters no logged-in player owns. It does this on your own cards, and on a player's card that comes from their own character. Blasts wait for you: use Resist all… (or Resist when there is one target).
b3.i5: Many targets. One card asks Defend or Resist for at most 12 of its targets; the others' owners get one notice to use the card's buttons.
b3.i6: Keep a GM logged in. Some of the players' actions are done by the GM's browser (without one they are told No GM is logged in to do this), and so are the Combat Turn and world-time timers, self-resisting NPCs and camera regions.
b3.i7: One GM, two windows. When the same GM account is logged in twice (a second tab, the desktop app beside a browser), each of these things happens once: the window opened first runs the timers and the cards that come by themselves, and the Defend and Resist prompts open in the window you used last. Everything you click works in the window you click it in. Close or reload a window and the other takes over within a few seconds.
b3.i8: Players' chat. A player's message keeps its colours and text styles, but anything that positions, sizes or hides parts of the screen is dropped.
b3.i9: What players can see. Foundry sends every chat message and every actor to every player's browser; whispers, blind rolls and NPC sheets you haven't shared are hidden in the interface only. A player who opens the browser's developer console can read them. Keep real secrets (a host's codes, a plot twist) in your own notes, not in the world.
b3.i10: The approval queue is a table rule, not a lock: its checks run in the player's browser.

houseRules.title: House rules and settings
houseRules.b1: Configure Settings, SR2e system: Edit house rules opens a window of rule values for this world, in sections: Tests and dice, Characters, Ranged combat, Gear, Magic and the Matrix, Street, Magic and critters, Initiative and actions, Melee, Vehicles and rigging, Building security, Upkeep, Tokens, GM tools, NPC generator, Time to get things (see Time), Safehouses and six Unified Rules Revamp sections, then Advanced (any other rule by its path, as JSON). Save applies the changes for everyone at once, and open sheets redraw by themselves.
houseRules.b2: Under each row are its default and changed when your value differs. With the Revamp as the rules source, the default shown is the Revamp's, and the rows it changes are marked with the book's value. A row above wins over the same path under Advanced. If the Advanced box isn't valid JSON, nothing is saved and the window stays open. Reset all to defaults clears your house rules for both rules sources. A house rule the system can't use (an unknown rule, or the wrong kind of value) is left out, and the GM gets a whispered list when the world loads.
houseRules.b3: The Find a rule… box at the top shows only the rows that match (and opens their sections); the links under it jump to a section. Click a section's title to fold it.
houseRules.b4: The rules changes made since v0.70.0 (dying out of combat, fresh pools at the start of a combat, holds, Take Aim, firing twice, Karma on contest cards, owned lifestyles, drone links, firmpoints and hardpoints, missiles, NPC ratings and many more) each have a switch here, a row or a value under Advanced, that puts the old way back. Search for the subject; many rows name the old choice (old).
houseRules.b5: Configure Settings itself is in sections:

b6.i1: GM and world: Edit house rules, Edit the Skill Web (defaulting links between skills), Players' purchases and Karma wait for the GM (the approval queue, off by default) and Support for Item Piles and Health Estimate (on; it needs a reload) and One look for module windows (on: with Foundry's dark colour scheme, each user's Monk's Enhanced Journal gets its own dark backgrounds once, where they are still at Monk's default).
b6.i2: Tokens and the map: Ward regions stop astral forms and Camera and sensor regions (see The GM panel), and each player's own Floating damage numbers, Turn pings and Pools on token hover.
b6.i3: Rolls, dice and chat: NPCs resist damage by themselves (see Chat cards for the GM), and each player's own roll privacy, dice colours and sound cues (off by default, with a volume and a sound file for each cue; the security alert cue is the GM's).
b6.i4: Other: Rules source (see the Unified Rules Revamp), Apply players' GM-only changes by themselves and each player's Dice So Nice: SR2e colours.
b6.i5: Look and layout: each player's own look (see Your look).

houseRules.b7: Many values were entered from memory and need checking against your SR2 rulebook: the list is docs/VERIFY.md in the project's source.

newEntry.title: New entries
newEntry.b1: Something the catalogue doesn't have (or there is no catalogue at all)? Make a new entry from your own book: New entry… in the shop (the Add window), in the SR2e tools window, or the GM panel's Setup tab.

b2.i1: Pick the Kind: weapon, armor, gear, cyberware, bioware, spell, adept power, focus, program or cyberdeck. The form shows the fields its stat line has, each with a hint.
b2.i2: Paste the stat line and press Read it: the name, numbers and codes fill the fields (damage like 9M, Availability like 4/48 hrs, ammo like 15(c), drain like (F/2)+1S, cost, Street Index and the rest in the book's column order). Check them: what was read and what wasn't is listed, and words it doesn't know are never kept.
b2.i3: The line under the form shows the entry as the shop will: what it is, its price and its Availability.
b2.i4: The Description is for your own words, not the book's text.

newEntry.b3: The GM saves it to the catalogue (ticked In the shop or not) and, opened from a sheet, can give it to that character. A player sends it to the GM: it waits in the GM panel's Requests tab, where Review… opens it to check and edit; saving it there approves it. Then anyone can find and buy it in the shop.
newEntry.b4: Nothing is shared outside your world. Templates and catalogue files hold what you typed from your books: keep them for your own group, and don't share or publish book text.

catalogue.title: The Catalogue
catalogue.b1: The Catalogue is a book of everything you can get: weapons, armor, gear, ware, foci, programs, decks, spells, adept powers, vehicles and drones, each with its own page. Open it from the SR2e tools window, the SR2e group of the left toolbar, the Catalogue button in the shop, or the round i beside a row in the shop (that row’s page).

b2.i1: Pick a tab, search, and tick the categories to show only those, as in the shop.
b2.i2: Click an entry to see its page: what it is, its category and where it is from; its price, Availability, Street Index and legality; its stats; and its description.
b2.i3: Buy… opens the shop at that entry (Learn… for a spell or an adept power opens the Add window).
b2.i4: The GM can open the item itself and tick In the shop on a page.

catalogue.b3: It lists what the shop reads: the GM’s catalogue, the system’s generic templates, world items and compendiums. Players see what the GM’s shop shows them (all of it, the catalogue only, or only what is marked in the shop).

sceneBuilder.title: Scene builder
sceneBuilder.b1: The Scene builder walks you through making a scene with everything in one place, then builds it in one go. Open it from the SR2e tools window (Alt+T), the toolbar's toolbox, the button in the Scenes sidebar, or New scene… at the top of the GM panel's Scene tab. Every step can be skipped, the column on the right shows what you have so far, and nothing is made until you press Build the scene.

b2.i1: Basics: the name, the folder, what kind of place it is (Real world, Astral or Matrix host), and its size in metres with the grid. The kind picks sensible defaults: an astral or Matrix scene is lit everywhere and gets its own backdrop, and a Matrix scene gets a host. Characters still project, perceive or jack in themselves, as on any scene.
b2.i2: Map: one of the backdrops drawn for the system (streets, an alley, a rooftop, a warehouse, an office floor, a club, sewers, a garage, docks, a forest, the astral plane, a host, the grid), a plain colour, or a picture of your own. A built-in backdrop brings its size and, ticked, walls, doors and lamps that match the picture. Token vision and fog of war are set here too.
b2.i3: Time and conditions: the time of day sets the darkness (day, dusk and dawn, night, darker in the wilds; indoors the lamps light it), or type your own darkness. The light level it gives is shown. You can also move world time to that hour (it asks first: every timer runs). Weather and the vehicle terrain are the Scene tab's settings.
b2.i4: Magic: background count and its sources, environment tags for totems, and a ward or barrier over the whole scene or the NPCs' area (a barrier actor and a region on the map).
b2.i5: Who's there: tick the player characters, then add NPCs, spirits and critters from your actors (the list, or drag them in from the Actors sidebar) or made by the NPC generator (a person, a group, a spirit, critters, each with a Threat Level; roll again to change them). Each row sets how many, whether they are hidden, their attitude (the token's disposition) and whether they are one morale group. Player characters start in one area of the map and everyone else in another. Copies of an actor are unlinked tokens; tick Unique for a named NPC whose sheet is the token's.
b2.i6: Security and Matrix: a host and a security site, either ones you have or made for the scene. A new site puts a maglock on the backdrop's secure doors, with cameras and an alarm rated by Threat; its host is the one above. On a Matrix scene the host's token stands on the map, and its IC arrives from its security sheaf as the tally climbs.
b2.i7: Finish: your notes, a GM journal entry (the notes, the summary and links to everything made), music, the combat tracker (everyone added to a new combat, and the NPCs' initiative rolled if you like), and whether to view the scene yourself or show it to the players.

sceneBuilder.b3: Opened on an existing scene (Change this scene… in the Scene tab, or Change with the Scene builder in a scene's menu in the sidebar), it starts from that scene's settings. What you change there is changed, and the people, ward, site and host you pick are added; nothing already on the scene is deleted, its size stays, and a backdrop's walls are only added to a scene with no walls yet.
sceneBuilder.b4: Save as a template (on the Finish step) keeps every choice, including who's there, so the same kind of scene takes one click next time: load it on the Basics step. Everything the builder makes is marked, so Remove this scene and what the builder made (it asks first) deletes the scene, the actors and journal it made for it and the combats on it, and leaves your own actors and journals alone.

spellFormulas.title: Spell formulas and teachers
spellFormulas.b1: Out of character creation a magician learns a new spell only from a spell formula they hold, from a teacher who knows it, from their magical group's grimoire, or from a spell they designed themselves. The learning test and the Good Karma are the same in every case.

b2.i1: Buying a formula: in the shop or the Add window, the scroll on a spell's row opens Buy a formula…. Pick the Force (you can learn the spell at up to it) and the tradition (hermetic or shamanic). A formula is gear: it is found, haggled, bought, sent to the GM's approval queue and delivered like anything else, and it can be given, traded or sold.
b2.i2: Learning from it: open the formula on your sheet and press Learn this spell…, or use Learn in the Add window: a formula you hold is used by itself. A spell you know at a lower Force is raised; raising a Force needs a formula of the new Force.
b2.i3: A teacher: the teacher icon by the Spells heading lists everyone in the world who knows a spell. The teacher rolls Instruction; their successes, up to their Sorcery, are extra dice for your learning test, rolled from the button on their card. A teacher no player plays charges a fee per point of Force.
b2.i4: The other tradition: a shamanic formula or teacher for a hermetic magician (or the reverse) works, but the learning test's TN is higher and the study takes longer.

spellFormulas.b3: The GM can switch every part of this off, or change its numbers, in the house rules (Magic and critters). All the numbers are the creator's interpretation, marked VERIFY until checked against the books.

interpretations.title: Rules interpretations (†)
interpretations.b1: Where the rules as written leave something unclear, the system uses the creator's reading and marks it with a small †: beside a value (the narrow Spell Pool dice on the strip) or as a line at the foot of a chat card. Hover a † for a one-line summary; click it to open Rules interpretations at that entry.

b2.i1: Each entry says what the rules leave unclear, how the system resolves it, and the sources.
b2.i2: Each names the house rule that changes it; the GM can open the house rules from there.
b2.i3: The whole list opens from the SR2e tools window (Rules interpretations).

interpretations.b3: They are interpretations, not rulings: the GM's call always wins.

resist.label: Resist the newest damage

initiative.hint: Rolls for your combatants who have no initiative yet in the current combat.

SceneBuilder.title: Scene builder

stepHint.basics: Name the scene, say what kind of place it is, and set its size and grid.
stepHint.map: Pick a backdrop drawn for the system, a plain colour, or a picture of your own.
stepHint.conditions: The time of day sets how dark it is; weather and terrain change the tests made here.
stepHint.magic: Background count, environment tags for totems, and a ward if the place has one.
stepHint.people: Who is on the map when it starts: player characters, and NPCs from your actors or made on the spot.
stepHint.security: A security site with locks, cameras and an alarm, and the Matrix host behind it.
stepHint.finish: Notes, a journal, music, the combat tracker, then build it. You can save the whole set-up as a template.

SceneBuilder.kindLegend: What kind of place is it?

kindHint.real: A place in the physical world: streets, buildings, the wilds.
kindHint.astral: The astral plane. Characters still project or perceive themselves; the scene gives the backdrop, background count and wards.
kindHint.matrix: The inside of a host. Deckers still jack in themselves; the scene gives the backdrop and the host.

SceneBuilder.editingScene: Changing {name}: what you add is added; nothing already on the scene is deleted.
SceneBuilder.templateNeedsName: Give the template a name first.

Interp.intro: Where the rules as written leave something unclear, the system uses the creator's reading. A † beside a value or on a chat card marks one; each is listed here with what is unclear, how it is resolved, the sources, and the house rule that changes it. All are open to the GM's call.
Interp.windowHint: Every interpretation the system uses, with its sources and house rule.

magicPoolLayers.title: The layered Magic Pool
magicPoolLayers.summary: Sorcery's concentration and specialization add Spell Pool dice usable only inside them.
magicPoolLayers.gap: The pool is sized by Sorcery, but the rules don't say what a concentration or specialization does to it.
magicPoolLayers.resolution: The pool comes in layers: Sorcery's rating for any magical action, then the concentration's extra dice only for actions inside it, then the specialization's only inside that. A test can use up to the rating it rolls; the Magic cap per test still holds; narrow dice are spent first.
magicPoolLayers.sources: SR2 Core pp. 70, 84–85; Awakenings p. 95; the Companion's split Karma Pools as precedent.

narrowCasting.title: Casting with a concentration or specialization
narrowCasting.summary: A spell inside Sorcery's concentration or specialization rolls that rating.
narrowCasting.gap: Other skills roll a concentration's or specialization's rating when it applies; the casting rules only name Sorcery.
narrowCasting.resolution: A casting or dispelling test inside the concentration or specialization rolls its rating, matched by name: a spell category, the spell's own name, or words such as Spellcasting, Spell Defense or Dispelling.
narrowCasting.sources: SR2 Core p. 70 (concentrations and specializations), pp. 84–85 (casting).

narrowDrain.title: Narrow dice for Drain
narrowDrain.summary: The narrow Spell Pool dice left may pay for that casting's Drain.
narrowDrain.gap: Spell Pool dice can go to the Drain test; with narrow dice it isn't said whether they may.
narrowDrain.resolution: Drain from a casting inside the concentration or specialization may use the narrow dice still left, then general dice.
narrowDrain.sources: SR2 Core pp. 84–85; the owner's decision.

formulaRequired.title: Learning needs a formula
formulaRequired.summary: Out of creation a new spell is learned from a formula, a teacher, the grimoire or a design.
formulaRequired.gap: How a character comes by a spell's formula after creation isn't laid out step by step.
formulaRequired.resolution: A player character out of creation learns a new spell only from a formula they hold (at that Force or more), a teacher, their group's grimoire or their own design; raising a Force needs a formula of the new Force.

formulaPrice.title: A formula's price and Availability
formulaPrice.gap: The numbers weren't checked against the book.
formulaPrice.resolution: Placeholder numbers the GM can change; marked VERIFY.

teacher.title: Learning from a teacher
teacher.summary: A teacher's Instruction successes, up to their Sorcery, add dice to the learning test.
teacher.gap: How much a teacher helps a spell's learning test isn't given as a number.
teacher.resolution: The teacher rolls Instruction (the training rule's skill and TN); the successes, up to their Sorcery, are extra dice for the student's own learning test; a teacher no player plays charges a fee per point of Force.
teacher.sources: SR2 Core (instruction and training); the owner's decision.

otherTradition.title: The other tradition's formula
otherTradition.summary: A formula or teacher of the other tradition works, but the test is harder and slower.
otherTradition.gap: How hard it is to learn from a hermetic formula as a shaman (or the reverse) isn't given as a number.
otherTradition.resolution: The learning TN + 2 and the study time × 2 (placeholders, VERIFY).

findRetry.title: Trying a failed find again
findRetry.summary: A find that fails can be tried again once its base time has passed.
findRetry.gap: When a failed Availability test may be rolled again isn't said clearly.
findRetry.resolution: Again after the item's base Availability time.

legalityFind.title: Legality when finding
legalityFind.summary: Restricted +2, Forbidden +4 to the find's TN, Forbidden twice the time.
legalityFind.gap: SR2's legality codes don't say how they change finding something.
legalityFind.resolution: Found openly, legality adds to the TN and the time (placeholders, VERIFY); a contact halves the row, a fixer drops it.

permits.title: Permits
permits.summary: A permit costs a share of the item's price and a wait.
permits.gap: The cost and time of a permit aren't given.
permits.resolution: 10% of the cost (at least ¥100; Restricted 25%, at least ¥500), 7 days (Restricted 30); placeholders, VERIFY.

contactHelp.title: A contact helping a find
contactHelp.summary: A contact helps as in legwork: closer contacts add dice, the contact can roll too.
contactHelp.gap: How a contact helps buying isn't laid out.
contactHelp.resolution: As legwork: a buddy +1 die, a friend for life +2, paid dice up to Loyalty, a favour +2 and no fee, the contact's own dice with the better result counting.
contactHelp.sources: SR2 Core (contacts, legwork); the owner's decision.

fixer.title: A fixer's find
fixer.summary: A fixer finds it with their own dice for a 10% cut and ×1.5 time.
fixer.gap: What a fixer charges and how long it takes isn't given.
fixer.resolution: The fixer's dice (or 2 per level), legality not counted, a 10% cut on the price, ×1.5 time, no haggling; a favour waives the cut. Placeholders, VERIFY.
